questions.question:
Will the Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication be pleased to state:
a) whether the Government has formulated a National Strategy for the transition toward next-
generation connectivity technologies, including 5G and future network infrastructure; and
b) if so, what are the key timelines, policy measures and investment plans envisaged for nationwide
deployment?
questions.reply:
(a) Yes, GoP has formulated a comprehensive national strategy for transition toward next generation
connectivity technologies, including 5G and future network infrastructure, through the Policy Directive for
IMT Spectrum Auction issued on 6th January 2026. The said Policy Directive is a key policy instrument
that not only establishes a long-term, technology-neutral and market-driven framework for spectrum
assignment and network evolution, but also incorporates wide-ranging telecom sector reform measures
aimed at strengthening digital infrastructure, improving sector efficiency, and facilitating investment. These
reforms include infrastructure sharing, rationalization of licensing framework, enhancement of affordability
through device ecosystem facilitation, promotion of local manufacturing, and improvement in sector
viability and service quality, along with crosssectoral interventions such as energy efficiency and dedicated
power solutions for telecom infrastructure. The overall objective is to accelerate digital transformation,
improve broadband penetration, and ensure inclusive and balanced nationwide connectivity. Furthermore,
phased network rollout and Quality of Service (QoS) enhancement plans have been incorporated as an
integral part of the newly issued licenses, ensuring structured deployment of next-generation services in
accordance with defined coverage, capacity, and performance benchmarks. The Government of Pakistan
under the vision of the Prime Minister has adopted a unified national policy to abolish Right of Way (RoW)
charges across all federal, provincial, and local jurisdictions to accelerate digital infrastructure deployment
and promote inclusive connectivity. Eliminating these charges will significantly reduce the cost and time
associated with laying fiber optic networks, incentivize private sector investment, and support the rapid
expansion of broadband services, particularly in underserved and remote areas. This reform aligns with

including 4G and 5G, enhancing ease of doing business, and fostering socio-economic development
through improved access to digital services nationwide. In this regard, amendments in Pakistan Telecom
Act have also being proposed and the enactment is in progress. To further promote innovation, digital
inclusion, and emerging technology ecosystems in line with GoP vision of digitalization, MoITT has
introduced policy and regulatory reforms including Mobile Virtual Network Operator (MVNO) Framework
approved in December 2025. The framework is expected to encourage service innovation, digital
entrepreneurship, niche-market connectivity solutions, and efficient utilization of existing telecom
infrastructure without requiring duplication of networks. The framework is also expected to support
specialized connectivity solutions for emerging sectors including Internet of Things (IoT), enterprise
services, smart applications, and digital platforms.
Moreover, MoITT is actively facilitating emerging connectivity technologies and future digital
ecosystems. In this regard, development of Satellite regulations and Fixed Satellite Services (FSS) licensing
framework is in progress and presently in finalization stage to support satellite broadband services and
expand connectivity in underserved and remote areas of the country. Similarly, spectrum management
reforms are also under consideration by MoITT and relevant stakeholders, including spectrum sharing and
spectrum reframing frameworks, aimed at promoting efficient spectrum utilization, improving network
capacity, and supporting future technology deployments including 5G and beyond. MoITT, through PTA,
is also facilitating frameworks for Internet of Things (IoT) and Short Range Device (SRD) services to
support emerging digital use-cases and smart infrastructure solutions as part of its broader digital
transformation agenda. In this regard, the IoT and SRD Framework was approved in 2023 to facilitate

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication be pleased to state the
expected impact of the newly introduced National Skill Competency Test for Information
Technology graduates on employment opportunities and export potential of Pakistan's Information
Technology sector?
questions.reply:
Pakistan produces a substantial number of ICT graduates each year; however, a persistent gap exists
between academic training and industry-required competencies, leading to variability in skill standards,
limited employer confidence, and constraints in scaling high-value IT exports.

To address this challenge, and in SXUVXDQFHRIWKH3ULPH0LQLVWHU¶VGLUHFWLYHVDPXOWLVWDNHKROGHU
Steering Committee was constituted in November, 2025 to oversee the planning, coordination, and
execution of the National Skill Competency Test (NSCT) for IT Graduates. The Committee, comprising
key stakeholders from HEC, MoITT, PSEB, P@SHA, NCEAC, and Virtual University, undertook a
comprehensive, time-bound, and coordinated exercise to operationalize this flagship national initiative.
NSCT is introduced as a standardized, competency-based assessment framework to benchmark
graduates against industry-aligned standards and provide objective certification of technical proficiency.
This initiative is centered on aligning computing education with industry needs, enhancing assessment
credibility, and improving graduates' employability. A competency framework with input of P@SHA was
developed for assessment.
The expected impact includes improved employability through verified skill validation,
establishment of a uniform national benchmark for IT competencies, enhanced international confidence in
Pakistani IT talent, greater participation of graduates in advanced technology domains such as AI, cyber
security, cloud computing and data science, and stronger industry-academia alignment²thereby
FRQWULEXWLQJWRLQFUHDVHGHPSOR\PHQWRSSRUWXQLWLHVDQGVWUHQJWKHQLQJ3DNLVWDQ¶V,7H[SRUWSRWHQWLDO
The NSCT was successfully conducted in April 2026 as a fully synchronized, computer-based test
across Pakistan, utilizing the Virtual University (VU) platform, reflecting a significant national scale, brief
details of the coverage and key statistics are given below;
x Universities Participated: ~190+
x Cities Covered: 112, Test Centers: 165
x Invigilation Staff Deployed by VU: 592 nationwide
x Registered Students: 40,784
x Students Appeared: 33,038 (Attendance: 81%)
x Sessions per Day: 04 (09:00 AM ± 04:30 PM)
x Total Questions: 100 | Duration: 120 minutes
x Monitoring Mechanism: HEC, MoITT, PAS (3rd Party Validation), P@SHA
The test has successfully:
x Generated credible, standardized national-level data for benchmarking CS/IT programs
x Established a verified national IT talent pool for industry access
x Strengthened academia±industry linkage through structured engagement
x Provided actionable insights for curriculum improvement and outcome-based education
Created a foundation for performance-based institutional evaluation and future funding linkages

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Poverty Alleviation and Social Safety be pleased to state:
a) whether it is a fact that, according to a recent assessment, poverty in Pakistan has substantially
increased, far higher than official government estimates, particularly in urban areas;
b) the year of data the Federal Government has relied upon for its poverty and social policy
formulation and the validity and reliability of such figures in reflecting the current situation;
c) the steps taken by the Government to strengthen social safety nets so that they effectively reach
the most vulnerable; and the measures being introduced; and
d) the extent to which funds of the Ministry are being utilized, to promote job creation, improve
economic mobility, and ensure equitable access to essential services, including education and
healthcare?
questions.reply:
(a)
BENAZIR INCOME SUPPORT PROGRAMME (BISP)

The statistical information regarding poverty estimates does not pertain to the Benazir Income
Support Programme (BISP) which operates through budgetary allocations released directly by the Finance
Division of Pakistan. The Finance & Accounts Wing of BISP maintains the official books of accounts,
which contain complete head-wise details of budget allocations and expenditures. Therefore, BISP can only
provide authenticated head-wise financial data and programme allocations; however, independent poverty
measurement and methodological assessments should be directed to the relevant statistical authorities and
research institutions.
PAKISTAN BAIT-UL-MAL (PBM)
Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal is not mandated with poverty assessment surveys; therefore no such data is
maintained by Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal.
TRUST FOR VOLUNTRY ORGANIZATION (TVO)
TVO does not independently conduct poverty assessments or surveys. The organization relies on
officially notified data and assessments of the Government of Pakistan, particularly those generated by the
Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS), for planning and
programmatic interventions.
PAKISTAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION FUND (PPAF)
Poverty estimation and official reporting fall under the mandate of the Ministry of Planning,
Development & Special Initiatives. PPAF does not undertake independent national poverty estimations and
relies on officially notified statistics for programmatic alignment. Any recent assessments or comparisons
with official estimates may therefore be clarified by the Ministry, which is responsible for methodological
frameworks and validation of poverty data.

(b) BENAZIR INCOME SUPPORT PROGRAMME (BISP)
The statistical information regarding poverty estimates does not pertain to the Benazir Income
Support Programme (BISP) which operates through budgetary allocations released directly by the Finance
Division of Pakistan. The Finance & Accounts Wing of BISP maintains the official books of accounts,
which contain complete head-wise details of budget allocations and expenditures. Therefore, BISP can only
provide authenticated head-wise financial data and programme allocations; however, independent poverty
measurement and methodological assessments should be directed to the relevant statistical authorities and
research institutions.
PAKISTAN BAIT-UL-MAL (PBM)
Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal is not mandated with poverty assessment surveys; therefore no such data is
maintained by Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal.
TRUST FOR VOLUNTRY ORGANIZATION (TVO)
TVO utilizes the most recent datasets and poverty estimates published by the Government of
Pakistan through relevant institutions, including BISP and PBS. The organization does not generate or
validate independent datasets and relies on the credibility and methodological rigor of official sources for
policy alignment and targeting of interventions,
PAKISTAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION FUND (PPAF)
The selection of datasets, reference years, and validation of poverty estimates used for policy
formulation are determined by the Ministry of Planning, Development & Special Initiatives. PPAF bases its
interventions on the officially available data and policy guidance. For details on the specific data sources,
reference periods, and their robustness in reflecting current socio-economic conditions, the Ministry may be
consulted.

(c) BENAZIR INCOME SUPPORT PROGRAMME (BISP)
BISP has expanded coverage of its core initiative i.e Unconditional Cash Transfer (UCT) to 10.2
million beneficiaries, and also increased quarterly cash assistance to Rs. 14,500. Further measures include
the rollout of Social Protection Wallet (SPW) Accounts for secure, transparent and direct payments,
particularly benefiting women, alongside Digital and Financial Literacy Training to promote effective use
of digital payments, financial management and inclusion. BISP in coordination with SBP is also in process

for enablement interoperability at POS agents and ATMs level so that beneficiaries could withdraw their
cash assistance as per their convenience.

organization of the Federal Government, working under Ministry of Poverty Alleviation and Social Safety.
Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal is operating number of programs/schemes for providing relief to the poor and
needy people in the field of education, free food and shelter, care for elderly persons, women
empowerment, child education and protection, food & shelter.
The details of such programs is as under:

emphasize livelihood support, small enterprise development, and community-level infrastructure, thereby

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination be pleased to state:
a) what mechanism have been adopted to ensure cross sector coordination and resource
mobilization under the National Drought Action Plan; and
b) how the Pakistan Drought Management System will provide real time monitoring and early
warnings to enable proactive, risk based drought management?
questions.reply:
(a) The Ministry of Climate Change & Environmental Coordination (MoCC&EC), being the focal
Ministry for drought-related matters under the Forestry Wing, has developed the National Drought Plan
(2025ʹ2035) with the technical support of the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification
(UNCCD). The Plan provides a comprehensive national framework and mechanism for drought risk
reduction through an integrated, multi-sectoral coordination mechanism. The key measures being adopted
are as follows:
i. Institutional Coordination Framework: Coordination among key federal and provincial
stakeholders including MoCC&EC, NDMA, PMD, Ministry of Water Resources, PARC,
Provincial Forest, Agriculture, Irrigation Departments and PDMAs.
ii. Five-Pillar Strategic Approach: (i) Assessment, Planning & Resource Mobilization, (ii) Policies,
Regulations & Governance, (iii) Monitoring & Early Warning Systems, (iv) Drought Response &
Mitigation, and (v) Capacity Building & Awareness.

iii. Integrated Planning & Budgeting: Mainstreaming drought management interventions into
PSDP/ADPs.
iv. Alignment with National & International Frameworks: Alignment with National Climate
Change Policy 2021, National Adaptation Plan 2023, National Water Policy 2018, SDGs, and UNCCD
commitments.
(b) The Pakistan Drought Management System (PakDMS) enables near real-time, nationwide
monitoring and forecasting of drought conditions by integrating satellite data, ground observations, and
climate model outputs into a unified decision- support platform. The system continuously monitors key
hydro- meteorological variables, including rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, vegetation health, and water

availability, at national, provincial, district, and tehsil levels. This provides decision-makers with timely
and spatially detailed insights, replacing reliance on delayed and fragmented reporting systems.
PakDMS consists of two core components:
1. Drought Monitoring Module
2. Drought Forecasting Module
1. Drought Monitoring Module
The monitoring module provides real-time assessment of current and historical drought conditions by
utilizing satellite-based remote sensing and available ground data.
This is particularly critical in data-scarce regions such as Balochistan, Sindh, Potohar, Tharparkar,
and Cholistan, where conventional monitoring networks are limited.
Key features include:
x Continuous tracking of drought indicators using satellite observations
x Spatially consistent coverage across all districts
x Early detection of meteorological, agricultural, and hydrological drought
The system computes 16 internationally recognized drought indices, including:
CWD, MAI, NDVI, SMCI, TCI, VCI, SMA, DrySpell, PCI, SPI (CHIRPS), SPI (ERA5L), RDI
(WaPOR),
ESI (WaPOR), NPP Anomaly (WaPOR), and VHI. These indices are generated dynamically using
cloud computing platforms (Google Earth Engine), ensuring timely updates and operational reliability.

2. Drought Forecasting Module
The forecasting module, developed under the WRAP project, introduces a forward-looking early
warning capability.
It integrates three key components:
x Satellite-based observations (current conditions)
x Sub-seasonal to seasonal climate forecasts
x Physically-based hydrological modeling
At its core is the Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) hydrological model, which translates
meteorological inputs into:
x Soil moisture
x Runoff
x Evapotranspiration
This enables the generation of spatially explicit drought forecasts with a lead time of up to 16 days,
aligned with operational decision-making needs in:
x Irrigation management
x Agricultural advisories
x Disaster preparedness
Operational Value for Early Warning
x Bridges data gaps in remote and underserved regions through satellite-based monitoring
x Provides continuous and comparable national coverage
x Detects early signs of drought before impacts become visible
x Supports anticipatory planning rather than reactive response
Institutional Coordination and Decision Support PakDMS is designed to support cross-sector
coordination among meteorological, water, agriculture, and disaster management institutions by providing a
shared, credible, and real-time evidence base.
This reduces uncertainty, enhances coordination between federal and provincial governments, and
enables timely interventions, such as:
x Water allocation adjustments
x Crop advisories
x Drought contingency planning

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination be pleased to state:
a) why unchecked Urban Sprawl particularly in Karachi, Lahore, and Rawalpindi continues to
strain infrastructure and worsen air quality, with Pakistan's urban population projected to reach
120 million by 2030 , yet the National Climate Change Policy lacks enforceable land-use regulations
to curb encroachment into agricultural zones;
b) whether air pollution now accounts for 22% of all deaths (over 135,000 annually), with Lahore
among the world's most polluted cities; and

c) whether the green urban planning framework is being developed under the National
Adaptation Plan to integrate affordable housing, public transport, green spaces and renewable
energy into a cohesive strategy to break the cycle of emissions-intensive, inefficient urban growth?
questions.reply:
(a) Unchecked urban sprawl in major urban centers such as Karachi, Lahore, and Rawalpindi is
driven by a combination of rapid urbanization, population growth, increasing housing demand, and
evolving socio-HFRQRPLFG\QDPLFV3DNLVWDQ¶VXUEDQSRSXODWLRQLVSURMHFWHGWRUHDFKDSSUR[LPDWHO\
million by 2030, which is placing significant pressure on infrastructure, transport systems, public services,
and environmental resources, including air quality.
The National Climate Change Policy 2021 recognizes urbanization, environmental degradation, and
air pollution as important climate-related challenges and emphasizes sustainable urban planning, green
infrastructure, climate-resilient development, and improved environmental management. However, land-
use planning and zoning regulation are primarily provincial and local government responsibilities under the
existing constitutional and administrative framework. Consequently, the Policy serves as a strategic and
guiding framework, while implementation of land-use controls and urban development regulations is
undertaken through relevant provincial laws, master plans, and development authorities. Ministry of
Climate Change is in close coordination with the Provincial Governments to provide the necessary
technical support to combat the climate-related challenges.
In this context, various provincial governments and development authorities are actively
strengthening planning and regulatory mechanisms to promote more structured and sustainable urban
growth. Initiatives include preparation of long-term master plans, implementation of land-use classification
and zoning rules, development of site development zone plans, promotion of compact and integrated urban
development models, and incorporation of environmental considerations into planning processes.
In addition, Pakistan Green Building Code initiatives are contributing towards environmentally
sustainable urban development through promotion of energy-efficient building design, water conservation
measures, improved waste management practices, natural ventilation systems, rooftop solar integration, and
resource-efficient construction materials. The Green Building framework also encourages climate-
responsive architecture, reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, and improved urban environmental
performance. These measures support sustainable urbanization by promoting efficient infrastructure
utilization and reducing environmental stress associated with expanding urban settlements.
Furthermore, measures relating to climate-resilient urban planning, environmental safeguards,
improved public transport planning, and enhanced coordination among planning, housing, and
environmental agencies are being progressively integrated into urban development frameworks. These
efforts are aimed at balancing urban expansion with protection of agricultural land, efficient infrastructure
utilization, environmental sustainability, and improved quality of life for urban residents.
Overall, the policy and institutional landscape continues to evolve towards more coordinated,
sustainable, and climate-responsive urban management through enhanced planning tools, regulatory
frameworks, green building standards, and inter-agency collaboration at federal, provincial, and local
levels.
(b) The National Clean Air Policy 2023 (NCAP) recognizes air pollution as an important public
health and environmental challenge, particularly in major urban centers of Pakistan. Available national and
international assessments, including findings referenced in the Global Burden of Disease Study 2019,
indicate that air pollution contributes significantly to disease burden and premature mortality in the country.
The Policy notes that approximately 135,000 premature deaths annually are associated with exposure to
ambient and household air pollution, including fine particulate matter (PM2.5). It also highlights that air
pollution may affect average life expectancy by up to 2.7 years.
With respect to Lahore, the NCAP identifies Lahore and adjoining areas as regions vulnerable to
seasonal smog and elevated particulate pollution levels, particularly during the winter months. Air quality
conditions in the broader Indo-Gangetic region are influenced by a combination of urban emissions,
industrial activity, vehicular movement, agricultural practices, construction activity, and seasonal
meteorological conditions.

The Government is actively implementing a comprehensive range of policy, regulatory, and
technical measures under the National Clean Air Policy 2023 and related environmental frameworks to
improve air quality and environmental sustainability. These measures include strengthening air quality
monitoring networks through installation and expansion of Air Quality Monitoring Systems (AQMS),
promotion of cleaner technologies and fuels, facilitation of electric mobility infrastructure, regulation of
industrial and vehicular emissions, urban greening and afforestation initiatives, and implementation of
smog management measures in major cities.
In addition, provincial governments, environmental protection agencies, and urban development
authorities are integrating environmental sustainability considerations into urban planning and
infrastructure development through green building initiatives, plantation campaigns, improved traffic
management, environmentally compliant construction practices, and promotion of energy-efficient urban
systems.
Furthermore, various development authorities including LDA, RDA, RUDA, and PHATA are
supporting sustainable urban development through planned infrastructure expansion, environmentally
responsive planning approaches, enforcement of development standards, and incorporation of
environmental safeguards within ongoing and future projects.

questions.question:

a) whether it is a fact that the Federal Employees Benevolent and Group Insurance Funds (FEB
and GIF) are not re-imbursing the educational fees for the children of Federal Government
employees enrolled in BS Engineering in National University of Science and Technology (NUST); and
b) if so, the reasons for non-reimbursement of fee?
questions.reply:
(a) No.
FEB&GIF in pursuance of Rule 25-A of the FEBF&GI Rules, 1972, makes reimbursement of educational
fees upto Rs. 100,000/- p.a. to the children of Federal Government employees, enrolled in BS Engineering
degree programs recognized and accredited by the Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC) and Higher
Education Commission (HEC), in any Public sector Institute on merit basis (Annex-A). National
University of Sciences and Technology (NUST) is a Public sector Institute and children of Federal
Government employees enrolled in BS Engineering degree programs (recognized and accredited by the
aforesaid authorities) in NUST on merit basis, are eligible for fee reimbursement.

(b) Not applicable.

The primary objectives of the spectrum auction were to ensure efficient allocation of scarce spectrum

All CMOs actively participated in the auction and collectively secured additional spectrum. As a result of

assignments in Pakistan (with a total of 754 MHz). This spectrum auction has placed Pakistan ahead of
other regional countries like India, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia and Bangladesh. This represents a
transformational leap in strengthening digital infrastructure, enabling enhanced network capacity, improved
quality of service, and accelerated 5G deployment across Pakistan. The process has also been widely
appreciated by all stakeholders, including bidders and international bodies such as ITU, APT and GSMA
etc, for its transparency and adherence to global best practices. In addition, strong market confidence and
operator appetite for next-generation services is reflected from the spectrum acquisition outcome itself,
wherein operators acquired approximately 480 MHz spectrum out of around 597 MHz spectrum offered in

acquisition strategies adopted by operators during the auction reflected commercial considerations, phased

(b) The rollout obligations have been carefully structured after extensive policy, technical, and
market deliberations to ensure that deployment of next-generation technologies remains balanced,

sustainable, and nationally inclusive, rather than concentrated only in commercially attractive urban
centers. The framework has specifically been designed to ensure progressive and equitable expansion of 5G
services across urban and rural areas, extending gradually to city and district level throughout the country.
In this regard, the licenses require that equivalent to 10% of existing 4G/LTE sites in each designated city
shall be upgraded/deployed for provision of 5G services each year in accordance with the phased rollout
framework. The phased approach ensures that across the four rollout phases, 5G services are progressively
expanded beyond Federal and Provincial capitals to additional cities nationwide. The required 5G rollout
on 10% of existing network sites within the first phase is an infrastructure-based deployment obligation and
forms part of the comprehensive rollout plan stipulated in the newly issued licenses. This obligation serves
as an initial trigger for service availability in priority areas, in line with the phased network expansion
framework. Recently issued licenses obligate the licensee, for a period of nine years from the effective date
of the license, to deploy at least 1,000 sites per year, of which a minimum of 200 must be entirely new
sites. The 4G sites shall be proportionately distributed between urban and rural areas in each province.
Furthermore, 5G coverage shall be rolled out in four phases, along with enhancement of the Fiber-to-the-
Site (FTTS) ratio of total network sites, as detailed in the table Attached at Annex-A.
Furthermore, enhanced Quality of Service (QoS) thresholds are also incorporated in said licenses,
data rate for 4G has been enhanced from 4 Mbps to 20 Mbps, with a further increase to 50 Mbps in a
phased manner. For 5G, data rate of 50 Mbps has been introduced, with an end-state target of 100 Mbps in
phased manner to ensure significantly improved network performance and user experience.
(c) The 15-year technology-neutral licenses issued after the recent NGMS/5G spectrum auction
include enhanced targets for rollout and quality of service (QoS) obligations in a phased manner, as
explained in (b) of the table attached at Annex-A. The rollout framework has specifically been designed
after detailed policy and technical deliberations to discourage concentration of next-generation services
only in commercially attractive urban centers and instead ensure progressive nationwide expansion of
advanced digital connectivity infrastructure. In this regard, rollout obligations require proportionate
distribution of 4G sites between urban and rural areas in each province, while the phased 5G deployment
framework ensures gradual expansion from Federal and Provincial capitals to additional cities across the
country over the four rollout phases. These licenses enable operators to not only improve existing 4G
networks but also deploy advanced technologies, and all operators have accordingly initiated rollout of 5G
services. The licenses require that 4G sites be proportionately distributed between urban and rural areas in
each province, whereas 5G rollout prioritizes Federal and Provincial capitals, including Islamabad,
Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar, and Quetta, in the first phase, followed by phased expansion to other major
cities. Data rate for 4G has been enhanced from 4 Mbps to 20 Mbps, with a further increase to 50 Mbps in a
phased manner. For 5G, data rate of 50 Mbps has been introduced, with an endstate target of 100 Mbps.
CMOs are currently in the process of procurement and import of equipment for establishment of new
4G/5G sites, and a visible improvement in coverage and QoS is expected within the next 4 to 6 months.

consultative measures to ensure affordability of 5G services. In this regard, a flexible and investment-
friendly spectrum pricing framework has been adopted, comprising one-year moratorium on spectrum fee
and an extended payment tenure. These measures are aimed at reducing the upfront financial burden on
operators, enabling cost-efficient network rollout and, ultimately, affordable telecom services for
consumers. PTA continues to foster a competitive and investment-friendly regulatory environment to
support affordable service offerings. Under the Mobile Tariff Regulation, 2025, the Authority regulates
tariffs to prevent excessive pricing and anti-competitive behavior, and retains the power to intervene where
consumer interests are adversely affected. Significant Market Power (SMP) operators are required to obtain
prior approvals for tariff revisions in line with regulatory provisions. In addition, under the merger
conditions, Ufone and Telenor are also required to take tariff approvals. All operators (both SMP and Non-

2004. Annual Performance Evaluation Reports of Government Servants are written by their Reporting Officers and
countersigned by the Countersigning Officers. The Federal Board of Revenue has recently implemented a 360 degree
evaluation system for its officers, details of which may be obtained from that organization. In view to 'further improve

strengthening and codifyitg the process of writing PERs, digital submission of PERs introduction of 360 degree evaluation
and others. These proposals are under consideration and will be finalised after due consultation and approvals.
(b) A number of steps have been taken in the past to modernize human resource management in the
Federal Bureaucracy. Recent initiatives include development of a Human Resource Management information
System (HRMIS) with continuous refinements and updations, design of software for digital submission of PERs.

operationalized.

criteria such as education qualifications, experience, age and grade. Upon submission of formal application,
cases are processed and with the approval of the competent authority under Rule 7(1) NOC to Apply are

obtain NOC to Avail such cases are placed before the Special Selection Board (SSB) in terms of Rule 5 (2)

3. BS-1 to 16 Secretary of the Ministry or Division

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination be pleased to state:
a) what steps are being taken by the Government to strengthen disaster preparedness and
resilience against climate-related events such as floods, droughts, and extreme heat-waves; and
b) what efforts have been made to secure international climate financing, grants, and technology
transfers to support Pakistan's Climate adaptation and mitigation initiatives?
questions.reply:
(a) To institutionalize climate resilience and prevent recurring disasters, the Government of
Pakistan has strengthened its policy and planning frameworks through key national instruments.
The Ministry of Climate Change & Environmental Coordination (MoCC&EC) is mandated to formulate,
coordinate, and oversee national policies and actions related to climate change, particularly climate
adaptation and resilience. It has undertaken several strategic initiatives to guide and mainstream climate
considerations into national and provincial development planning. These include:
National Climate Change Policy 2021 ± updated to align national priorities with emerging climate
challenges.
Pakistan Climate Change Act 2017- provides a legal framework for mitigating and adapting to
Climate Change
Nationally Determined Contributions ± supporting mitigation and adaptation actions in line with
global commitments.
Monsoon 2026 Strategic Plan: Approved by the PM in November 2025, the Plan delineates short,
medium, and long-term goals for flood preparedness, resilience, and recovery mechanisms.
Framework for Implementation of Climate Change Policy (2014±2030) ± a roadmap for sectoral
climate actions across the country.
National Communication on Climate Change ± reporting progress and commitments under the
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.
Mainstreaming gender considerations in all climate action programs.
MoCC&EC is also working to strengthen institutional coordination, enhance climate finance access,
build provincial capacity, and promote research, awareness, and early warning systems to deal with
evolving climate risks.
Major National Climate Initiatives
To respond to these challenges, several ongoing and planned initiatives offer scalable models:
SAFER Project (by MoCC&EC and International Center for Integrated Mountain Development,
funded by Adaptation Fund): focuses on integrated watershed management, nature-based recharge systems,
wetlands rehabilitation, climate-resilient WASH systems, cryosphere risk management, and early warning
systems across Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Sindh²aligning with the National Adaptation
Plan and Living Indus Initiative.
The GIZ-funded Strengthening Climate Adaptation and Resilience (SAR) project in Pakistan
(2021±2025) supports the government in enhancing climate resilience through risk assessments, planning,
and financing. It focuses on building the capacity of public and private partners to implement climate
adaptation measures in sectors like agriculture, water, and health.

Upscaling Green Pakistan Program (UGPP): builds on the Ten Billion Tree Tsunami Program to
finance check dams, sediment traps, and forest landscape restoration through Public Sector Development
Program funding.
Buner and Shangla Early Warning Project (by World Food Program): installs hydromet stations,
river monitoring, and community-based early warning systems in glacier-prone mountainous areas.
District Adaptation Plans/Locally Led Adaptation Plans: In order to bolster the resilience of the
vulnerable communities, district adaptation plans are in process.
Coordination with the Provinces: The Ministry keeps liaison with the provinces, issues advisories,
and engages them in capacity-building and training, under the umbrella of NAP.

Other cross-cutting supportive policy and financing instruments include:
x ESG Guidelines by SECP for Listed Companies ± Promote ESG disclosure and climate risk
integration in corporate practices.
x Carbon Market Trading Guidelines 2024 by MoCC&EC ± Enable carbon credit generation and
trading to mobilize climate finance.
x Green Banking Guidelines by State Bank of Pakistan ± Encourage banks to finance green and
climate-resilient projects.
x Environmental and Social Risk Management Framework by State Bank of Pakistan ± Integrates
environmental and climate risk into financial lending decisions.
x Green Finance Taxonomy by State Bank of Pakistan and MoCC&EC ± Defines and classifies
green and climate-aligned investments.
x Climate Hazard and Impact Risk Assessment by Planning Commission ± Screens public
development projects for climate risks.
Post Disaster Need Assessment (PDNA) pertains to the Ministry of Planning, Development and
Special Initiatives.
To address drought and agricultural vulnerability, the Indus Basin Climate Resilient Agriculture and
Water Management Project ($47.7 M, FAO, 2020±2026) is deploying state-of-the-art technology to build
adaptive capacity against climate impacts on agriculture and water systems in Punjab and Sindh, benefitting
17.3 million people. The Combating Land Degradation through Integrated Range and Livestock
Management Project (GEF, $15.2 M, FAO) is reversing land degradation in grassland and scrub forest
ecosystems in northern Punjab directly addressing drought-related land stress while increasing carbon
sequestration, climate resilience, and food security in Attock, Chakwal, and Jhelum districts.

(b) Pakistan has made substantial and sustained efforts to mobilize international climate
financing, grants, and technology transfers through active engagement with multilateral climate funds,
development finance institutions, and international implementing agencies. Through the Green Climate
Fund (GCF), Pakistan has successfully secured 11 approved projects ($331.9 million), making it one of the
more active GCF recipient countries in the region. These projects span climate adaptation, disaster risk
reduction, clean energy and water infrastructure. In parallel, through the Global Environment Facility
(GEF), Pakistan has secured 4 projects with GEF financing of $11.3 million, covering biomass energy,
low-carbon circular economy, land degradation, and sustainable agricultural value chains. On technology
transfer specifically, the Indus Basin Climate Resilient Agriculture Project (FAO, $47.7 M) is deploying
state-of-the-art climate information and water management technologies across Punjab and Sindh; the
Pakistan Distributed Solar Project (JS Bank, $54 M, GCF) is mobilizing tailored financing solutions to
bridge the investment gap for distributed solar PV technology; and the Accelerating Low Carbon Circular
Economy through Clean Tech Innovation Project (UNIDO, $11.8 M, GEF) is facilitating investments in
clean technologies integrating renewable energy, energy efficiency, and waste management. The details of
projects under GCF and GEF to secure international climate finance are attached at Annex-I.

(Annexure has been placed in the National Assembly Library)

SAEED AHMAD MAITLA
Acting Secretary

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Poverty Alleviation and Social Safety be pleased to state:
a) whether it is a fact that there are cases pending in litigations relating to the claims of different
firms against Benazir Income Support Programme regarding survey Reports of Southern Punjab
etc;
b) if so, the details, names of the firms, amount of contracts and reasons for terminating the
contracts of the pending litigations cases during the last three years?
questions.reply:
(a) Yes, it is a
fact that a case is pending in litigation regarding the claim of a firm against the Benazir Income Support
Programme (BISP), arising out of survey operations in Southern Punjab.
It is apprised that BISP carried out door-to-door surveys for its National Socio-Economic Registry
(NSER) in 2010±11 and again in 2018±22, by engaging private Partner Organizations (POs) in accordance
with PPRA rules. The 2018±22 survey was done to update the data collected through 2010±11 survey.
During the 2018±22 survey the country was divided into eight clusters, with Southern Punjab falling under
Cluster±3. The contract for the Cluster-3 was awarded to M/s Sustainable Development Policy Institute
(SDPI) under an agreement signed on 26.03.2019.
Although SDPI completed the required enumeration targets, BISP imposed penalties due to various
discrepancies and contractual violations. SDPI challenged the imposition of these penalties and initiated
arbitration proceedings under the Arbitration Act, 1940. The proceedings commenced in November 2024
and are currently at the evidence stage.
(b) The contract with M/s Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI), for the door-to-
door survey in Southern Punjab (Multan, D.G. Khan, and Sahiwal Divisions) under the NSER update
Survey (2018-22), amounted to PKR 1,042,179,849/- for 4,411,426 households.

The contract was not terminated; rather, it expired on 31.12.2022. Due to coverage and quality
deficiencies, BISP released PKR 792,056,686/- for six milestones, against the total invoiced amount of
PKR 1,042,179,849/- for eight contractual milestones, while an amount of PKR 250,123,164/- for two
milestones was withheld on account of penalties.
The matter arises from contractual violations, including submission of incorrect survey data and
non-compliance with agreed standards. No criminal case was registered, as the violations were contractual
in nature. SDPI challenged the penalties by initiating arbitration proceedings under the Arbitration Act,
1940 in November 2024 which are currently sub-judice. Further action shall be taken in light of the final
award of the learned arbitrator and the matter is being actively pursued to safeguard public funds.

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination be pleased to state:
a) whether it is a fact that the childhood cancer survival rate in Pakistan is below 30% as compared to over
80% in the higher income countries; if so, the details thereof;
b) the reasons for this disparity including delays in diagnosis, shortage of trained specialists, limited access
to specialized treatment centers and high treatment costs;
c) the steps taken to raise awareness among the public and healthcare providers for early diagnosis and
timely referral to oncological centers;
d) whether the Government has any initiatives to improve the availability and affordability of childhood
cancer treatment particularly in remote and underserved areas; and
e) the details as any timeline and measures adopted to establish more specialized treatment centers and
enhance medical training in order to improve childhood cancer survival rates in the country?
questions.reply:
(a) Yes,
in high-income countries, childhood cancer survival exceeds 80%, whereas in low- and middleincome countries,
including Pakistan, it is often below 30% (World Health Organization, 2023).
(b) Reasons for the Disparity
The lower survival rates are primarily due to systemic clinical, and socioeconomic factors, including:
1. Delays in Diagnosis: Late presentation is common due to:
- Low awareness among caregivers
- Weak referral systems
. Limited screening/early detection
Leads to diagnosis at advanced stages, reducing survival chances
2. Shortage of Trained Specialists: Limited number of:
* Paediatric oncologists
* Oncology nurses
* Support staff
* Affects quality and continuity of care
3. Limited Access to Specialized Treatment Centers
. Services concentrated in a few urban tertiary hospitals
Rural populations face:
* Geographic barriers
Travel/logistical constraints
4. High Treatment Costs & Financial Barriers: Out- of-pocket expenditure remains high that leads to:
- Treatment delay
Treatment abandonment (major issue in LMICs)
5. Treatment Abandonment: A major contributor in Pakistan is linked to
- Poverty
- Lack of social support
Distance from treatment centers
6. Weak Health System & Supportive Care: Limited:
- Diagnostic facilities
- Infection control
Blood banks / ICU support
Increases treatment complications and mortality

The disparity in childhood cancer survival is primarily attributable to delays in diagnosis, shortage of trained
; specialists, limited access to specialized treatment facilities, and high treatment costs. Additional contributing
factors include treatment abandonment, weak referral systems, and inadequate supportive care infrastructure. These
challenges are well documented by the World Health Organization and global oncology initiatives.
(c) The steps taken to raise awareness among the public and healthcare providers for early diagnosis and
timely referral to oncological centers; In order to strengthen early diagnosis and timely referral cases i for cancer
care, efforts are underway to train frontline
;
healthcare workers to refer these cases. The development of
standardized guidelines, is underway with the support of the World Health Organization.
Furthermore, a comprehensive awareness-raising plan covering all non-communicable diseases (NCDs),
including : cancers, is being incorporated into the PC-1 submitted by the ; Ministry of National Health Services,
Regulations and Coordination (M/o NHSR&C) under the Diabetes Prevention initiative. This approach aims to
enhance public awareness as well as improve the capacity of healthcare providers for early detection and appropriate
referral to oncological centers.
(d) The Government has undertaken several initiatives to improve Tie availability and affordability of
childhood cancer treatment, particularly in remote and underserved areas.
Recently, the Ministry of National Health Services, ; Regulations and Coordination (M/o NHSR&C), in collaboration
with Roche Pakistan, has initiated a project covering cancer patients of ICT, AJK, and GB for the provision ci free
cancer medicines to eligible patients.
In addition, efforts are underway to work with the World Health Organization and St Jude Children's
Research Hospital to support capacity building, improve access to -essential medicines, and enhance service delivery
for childhood cancer care. These initiatives collectively aim to reduce the financial burden on patients and ensure
equitable
:
access to treatment across underserved regions.
Furthermore, a dedicated cancer hospital in Pakistan Institute; of Medical Sciences is nearing completion.
Under the Prime Minister’s directive, the Jinnah Medical Complex is being established to provide quaternary
care services, including specialized oncology care, to the residents of ICT and adjoining provinces/areas. The project
is planned to completion by 2028.
In parallel, efforts are also focused on capacity building and medical training through collaborations with
international partners, aimed at strengthening clinical expertise and (improving overall childhood cancer care
outcomes in the country.

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination be pleased to state:
a) the number of incidents of interruption in the supply of medicines or shortages of medicines reported in
Federal hospitals during the last five years;
b) the reasons for shortage of medicines;
c) whether the Government has examined the role of counterfeit medicines mafia or the lack of
transparency in the tendering process, causing this issue; and
d) the steps being taken by the Government to resolve this issue permanently?
questions.reply:
(a) a. No
systematic or prolonged interruption in the supply of medicines has been reported in Federal Government
Hospitals/institutes during the last five years. The hospital authorities ensure the uninterrupted availability of
essential life-saving medicines through proactive procurement planning and rigorous stock monitoring. While the
genera supply chain remained robust, minor and temporary coated shortages occurred in isolated instances. There
were primarily restricted to Quote-Controlled items or specialized medicines with a sole manufacturer dependency.
In all such cases patient care was prioritized through immediate alternate procurement arrangements.
(b) Occasional and temporary shortages are generally attributed to external and systemic factors. Limited
availability due to reliance on sole manufacturers for specialized and lifesaving medicines Necessary processing
times for import approvals and quota allocations for controlled substances.
Limited bidder interest in tenders for highly specialized items with low consumption volumes. External
factors such as supply chain constraints Acting availability at the national or international level.
(c) The Federal Government Hospitals / institutes maintains a "Zero Tolerance" policy toward counterfeit
medicines All procurements are strictly conducted under PPRA Rules, ensuring open competitive bidding and merit-
based selection. Every batch is accepted "on Provision of warranty certificates DRAP-registered manufacturers. A

Multi-Tiered Technical Scrutiny Committee evaluates every bid to ensure compliance with quality standards,
effectively eliminating the risk of substandard or counterfeit products entering the hospital supply chain.
(d) Measures taken at hospital level are strictly followed as per laid down DRAP rules where drug
sampling is done from medical stores by Drug Inspectors as per routine.

MULTAN, were in the Persian Gulf and unable to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Subsequently, pursuant to diplomatic
arrangements, MT. KARACHI was permitted eastbound passage on 15 March 2026 and is presently engaged in
crude oil lifting for refinery requirements. However, MT. Lahore and MT. Khairpur were not stranded (due to)
ongoing escalations in the Strait of Hurmuz. These two vessels continue to remain within the region, pending further
operational instructions and approval. Further, Karachi Gateway terminal has not suspended new export bookings
for Gulf destinations.
b). PNSC, in the light of prevailing geopolitical situation, insurance premiums, particularly war risk and
associated covers are subject to daily revision by underwriters. Correspondingly, freight rates have experienced a
substantial escalation, increasing up to five fold as compared to normal market conditions.

c). PNSC has confirmed that, in coordination with Abu Dhabi National Oil Company and Saudi Aramco,
local refineries have explored and utilized alternative crude loading origins, including Yanbu, Kingdom of Saudi
Arabia, and Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, to ensure continuity of supply. In addition, Karachi Port
Trust (KPT) and Port Qasim Authority (PQA) have proactively adopted complementary measures to safeguard
uninterrupted supply chains, mitigate cascading costs, and protect exporters in the evolving geopolitical environment:
 Alternative Shipping Routes (KPT):
 Feeder services launched via KGTL (AD Ports Group), including Pakistan Feeder Service (KFK)
and India–Pakistan Feeder Service (FKI), ensuring regional connectivity despite Strait of Hormuz
risks.
 KICT has facilitated reefer container movements, while Oman’s ASYAD is engaged for a proposed
Karachi–Sohar feeder link.
 Tariff Relief (PQA):
 Port charges already reduced by 50% under Ministry of Maritime Affairs Notification No.
2(4)/2021-PQA dated 1 July 2025.
 Proposal for an additional 10% reduction in wharfage charges for food export cargo at QICT,
FAP, and Marginal Wharf (MW), subject to Board and Ministry approval under section 13(4) of the
PQA Act, 1973.
Policy Alignment: These measures reflect the vision of the Honorable Prime Minister and Minister for
Maritime Affairs to facilitate trade, lower logistics costs, and strengthen Pakistan’s export competitiveness.

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination be pleased to state:
a) whether Ministry intends to frame rules and regulations for the public and private health sector to
require doctors and pharmacists to prescribe medicines by generic formula name instead of brand name;
b) whether there are any rules framed by the Government to regulate the pharmacies in Pakistan?
questions.reply:
(a) The
Ministry of NHSR&C is cognizant of the importance of prescription of medicines by generic names; however, this
may require addressing other associated aspects, in a phasic-manner. By adopting a gradual approach, the Ministry
intends to overcome the barriers that may come along; including availability of generic medicines across the region,
limited accessibility, prices variations, financial implications and multiple stakeholders in the sector who would be
requiring orientation/ training ensuring a smooth transition with vigilant monitoring and regulatory oversight in
place.
This matter of prescribing medicines by generic (formula) name has been thoroughly examined in
consultation with the relevant regulatory bodies.
The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan regulates registration, licensing, pricing and quality assurance of
therapeutic goods at the federal level under its Act. However, after the 18th Constitutional Amendment, health
service delivery and regulation of medical practice primarily fall within the jurisdiction of the provinces.
The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) issued formal communications to professional
associations (PMA) and provincial health departments on 16th April 2021, highlighting citizens' concerns regarding
company-influenced brand-based prescriptions. DRAP emphasized that brand-based prescribing increases the
financial burden on patients and contravenes the Code of Ethics for medical and dental practitioners.
DRAP has directed all stakeholders to take necessary measures to promote generic prescriptions and discourage
incentivized prescribing in the best interest of patients and the country. The phasic approach will be followed to
gradually adopt generic prescription.
(b) The sale of drugs is being regulated by the respective provincial governments by virtue of section 6 of
the Drugs Act, 1976.
In ICT, the drug sale establishments (pharmacies, Medical Stores and Distribution set-up) are being regulated
in accordance with the provisions of the ICT Drug Sale Rules. 2013 notified under the provisions of the Drugs Act,
1976, whereas all other provinces have their own notified Drug Sale Rules to regulate the pharmacies in their
territorial jurisdiction.

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination be pleased to state:
a) whether it is a fact that Pakistan currently relies almost entirely on the imported Antiretroviral Therapy
(ART) medicines largely procured through foreign funding;
b) whether it is also a fact that no ART medicines are being produced locally; if so, the reasons thereof; and
c) the measures adopted by the Government or steps being taken to promote local manufacturing of HIV
medicines and reduce dependence on external suppliers and donor funded procurement?
questions.reply:
(a) Yes, it is a fact that Pakistan currently relies predominantly on imported Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)
medicines. These medicines are largely procured through international funding mechanisms, including support from
global partners such as the Global Fund. Procurement is undertaken through the United Nations Development
Programme (UNDP) to ensure transparency and compliance with international standards. This modus through an
international pooled procurement mechanism offering access to competitive market terms and prices, ensures a
regular supply of WHO-prequalified, quality- assured medicines for People Living with HIV (PLHIV) enrolled in the
national treatment program.

(b) Pakistan has a well-established local manufacturing capacity for antiretroviral therapy (Art) medicines.
Currently, approximately 400 ART products are registered for local manufacture by various pharmaceutical
companies in the country. In addition, 26 ART brands are registered as imported products. This reflects that ART
medicines are registered for local manufacturing to fulfil the country’s requirements while imports also supplement
availability to ensure adequate access to these essential medicines.

(c) The Government has undertaken measures to promote local manufacturing of HIV medicines and
reduce reliance on external suppliers and donor-funded procurement. In this regard, antiviral drugs, including
antiretroviral therapy (ART) medicines, are given priority in regulatory review and approval. This facilitation is in
line with the decision of the Registration Board in its 257th
meeting held on 24-25 Marh, 2016, aimed at expediting
the availability of these critical medicines through local production.

(a) The Federal Government has not
formulated a standalone, uniform “Water Pricing Policy” applicable across all sectors. This position is consistent
with the constitutional framework following the 18th Amendment, under which irrigation, agriculture, and water
supply for domestic and industrial uses fall within the jurisdiction of the Provinces.
However, the Government has formulated the National Water Policy, 2018 (NWP), duly approved by the
Council of Common Interests (CCI), which provides an overarching national framework. The Policy explicitly
recognizes water pricing as a key instrument for sustainability and stipulates:
“Adequate water pricing (Abiana) for irrigation and proper operation and maintenance of the irrigation
system as well as other user sectors. ’’ (Section 2.17)
Thus, while a centralized pricing policy has not been framed, a nationally agreed policy direction on water
pricing exists within the NWP framework.
(b) A uniform national implementation is neither envisaged nor constitutionally appropriate.
The National Water Policy, 2018 clearly provides a decentralized implementation mechanism, stating:
“Within the broad parameters of water security, as stipulated in NWP-2018, the Provincial Governments
can formulate more detailed policies and guidelines on subjects like (i) water pricing (ii) drinking water, (Hi) water
quality and (iv) water treatment. ” (Section 3.7)
Accordingly, Provinces determine water tariffs and pricing structures for agricultural, industrial, and urban
uses in line with their respective socio-economic conditions, resource availability, and administrative frameworks.
The NWP further provides differentiated guiding principles for various sectors, including:
• Cost recovery for productive uses such as agriculture and industry '
• Affordability considerations for drinking water and sanitation
• Rationalization of tariffs to ensure sustainability
Therefore, the absence of uniformity reflects a deliberate, policy-backed and constitutionally aligned
approach, rather than a gap in implementation.
(c) Yes, revenue is generated through water charges (Abiana), urban water tariffs, and industrial usage
fees as determined by the respective Provincial Governments and relevant service delivery agencies.
However, the National Water Policy acknowledges that water is presently underpriced, and existing
recoveries generally meet only a limited portion of the Operation and Maintenance (O&M) costs of water
infrastructure. This gap necessitates progressive tariff reforms and improved cost recovery mechanisms to ensure
sustainability.
(d) The Government's planning for financial protection and long-term sustainability of water resources is
comprehensively articulated in the National Water Policy, 2018, which provides a structured and balanced
framework.
At the outset the Policy establishes water pricing as a core national objective:
"Adequate water pricing (Abiana) for irrigation and proper operation and maintenance of the irrigation
system as well as other user sectors. ” (Section 2.17)
This objective is operationalized through the following key provisions:
1. Economic and Financial Sustainability (Section 25.1 & 25.2)
“The delivery services of water for all its uses shall be made economically and financially sustainable and
the social, as well as economic value, of water shall be emphasized. ” (Section 25.1)
“Water at the delivery point shall be realistically priced according to a general principle that
For production sectors of the economy, full cost recovery shall be effected;
For social uses, the concept of affordability shall be applied;
For environmental and ecological needs, water supply shall be free of cost. ” (Section 25.2)
2. Targeted Subsidy Framework (Section 25.3)
“Wherever subsidy becomes inevitable, it shall be carefully estimated and the source of its financing would
be clearly indicated... The extent of subsidy shall be periodically reviewed and adjusted. " (Section 25.3)

3. Irrigation Water Pricing and Sustainability (Section 10.12)
“Water is a highly underpriced commodity in Pakistan. The prevailing cost recovery through water charges
(Abiana) is able to meet only a fraction of the O&M cost of the irrigation infrastructure. Measures are required to
enhance the water charges to realistic extent to meet the O&M cost of the infrastructure and to ensure long-term
sustainability. ” (Section 10.12)
4. Urban Water Financial Sustainability (Section 12.2)
“Full financial sustainability shall be aimed at for the Urban Water Supply and Sanitation Systems...
Similarly, urban water tariffs must be revised to ensure financial sustainability. ” (Section 12.2)
5. Demand Management (Section 26)
“Demand Management of various uses shall, therefore, he accorded high priority. ” (Section 26)
It is further added that the MoWR has been requesting provinces to take immediate steps on revising water
tariffs for urban and agricultural consumers, with effective safety- nets for the low-income consumers (Annex-Ill).
The provinces have accordingly revised their water tariffs. Notifications may be seen at Annex-IV.
(Annexures have been placed in the National Assembly Library)

sl

questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Food Security and Research be pleased to state:
a) why wheat and sugar crises repeatedly occur in the country; and
b) what Institutional reforms have been adopted for their prevention?
questions.reply:
(a) Wheat and sugar are
essential food commodities. Production depends mainly on crop yield/productivity, availability of quality inputs
(seed, fertilizers, irrigation water), cliiiiatic conditions, and prices of produce. Due to increasing impacts of climate
change, crop yields and sucrose levels are adversely affected, and Pakistan's pcr- hectare yield remains significantly
below global averages.

Pakistan is the 5th most populous country with a population growth rate of around 2.5% per annum.
However, production has not kept pace with rising demand, resulting in occasional demand-supply gaps and

crises.
The Government adopts proactive measiti es. including timely imports where necessary.
(b) The Government has undertaken several institutional reforms and policy mcasiires. including:

• Revamping of Pakistan .Agricultural Research Council (PARC).
• fransition to a market-based system through Interim National Wheat Policy 2025- 26.
• Reforms in PASSCO and Provincial flood Departments.
• Establishment of National Wheat flvei sight
Committee (NWOC) to ensure coordination and maintenance of strategic reserves.
• Deregulation and liberalization of the wheat sector.
• Removal of price controls and abolition ca1 movement restrictions.
• Introduction of track and trace system the sugur sector.
• Encouraging private sector participation in procurement, storage, and trade.
Promotion of modern storage facilities to reduce post-harvest losses
Further measures include: Constitution of a committee under directions of the Hon'ble Prime Minister to
ensure uninterrupted inter- provincial movement of certified wheat seed (Rabi 2025—26), resulting in 35%
increase in certified seed usage (Annex-I)
• Regular meetings of NWOC to m o nit or y implementation.
• Strengthening procurement through transparent processes under PPRA rules.
• Reinforcement of research linkages for climate- resilient, high-yielding varieties.
• Improved availability of critical inputs across provinces.
Ongoing reforms under National Agri- Biotechnology Policy and National Seed Policy.

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination be pleased to state what
strategy is being evolved to advance vaccine self-reliance, strengthening vaccine manufacturing capabilities
within the country in view of Covid-19 pandemics and subsequent global supply disruptions?
questions.reply:
1. Four vaccines are currently produced in Pakistan through fill-and-finish operations.
2. In April 2025, the Ministry of National Health Services Regulations & Coordination launched an initiative to
advance indigenous vaccine manufacturing, focusing on demand assessment, cost optimization, local
production feasibility, and policy incentives.
3. To ensure an inclusive and evidence-based approach, 23 structured consultative sessions were conducted
with key stakeholders, including international partners, government entities, industry representatives, as well
as engagements with health authorities of Indonesia and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
4. These efforts have led to the development of a comprehensive draft National Policy for Advancing
Indigenous Vaccine Production, outlining a phased and time-bound framework across the full value chain
from R&D to manufacturing and distribution supported by regulatory strengthening, localization, fiscal
incentives, and investment facilitation.
5. The draft policy has been approved by the Prime Minister and is being submitted to the Federal Cabinet for
final approval.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Railways be pleased to state:
a) by when tracking devices for locomotives and rolling stock and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)
tags under the Railway Advanced Infrastructure Network (RAIN) Phase-I will be made fully operational; and
b) how these technologies will improve safety, punctuality, asset management and provision of free public
Wifi at major stations?
questions.reply:
(a) Operationalization of Tracking Devices &
RFID under RAIN Phase-I
Under the Railway Advance Infrastructure Network (RAIN) Phase-l, the deployment of tracking devices for
locomotives and rolling stock, along with Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tags, is currently in advanced
stages of implementation.
These systems are planned to be operationalised by June 2026.
Once operationalised, these technologies will enable end-to-end visibility of railway assets across the network.
(b) Improvement in Safety
The integration of GPS tracking and RFID systems will significantly enhance operational safety by:
 Enabling real-time tracking of train movement

 Reducing the risk of collisions and operational conflicts
 Supporting Al-based monitoring systems at control centers
 Allowing quick response in case of emergencies or incidents
This ensures proactive safety management rather than reactive measures.
Enhancement of Punctuality
These technologies will directly contribute to improved train punctuality by:
 Providing live location data of trains across the network
 Enabling better scheduling and dispatch decisions
 Reducing delays through real-time monitoring and alerts
 Supporting centralized control rooms for traffic optimization
As a result, adherence to train schedules will improve significantly.
Strengthening Asset Management
RFID and tracking systems will help improve asset management by:
 Offering complete visibility of rolling stock (wagons, coaches, locomotives)
 Reducing asset misplacement and idle time
 Enabling predictive maintenance through data analytics
 Improving utilization of available resources

This will lead to cost optimization and increased operational efficiency.
Support for Free Public Wi-Fi at Major Stations
The deployment of optical fiber infrastructure under RAIN forms the backbone for multiple digital services,
including free public Wi-Fi. These technologies contribute by:
 Providing high-speed connectivity through fiber backbone
 Enabling seamless integration between stations and central systems
 Supporting passenger services such as:
o Online ticketing (RABTA)
o Real-time train information
o Digital communication platforms
Free Wi-Fi at major stations enhances passenger experience, promotes digital inclusion, and aligns Pakistan
Railways with global standards.

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination be pleased to state:
a) whether it is a fact that there has been a delay in the registration of life-saving diagnostic and medical
equipment in Pakistan; and
b) the number of applications currently pending and the reasons for delay in their approval by the Drug
Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP)?
questions.reply:
(a) The
registration of medical devices is governed by the Medical Devices Rules (MDR), 2017.
Previously, a manual, paper-based system was in place. This required the physical submission of dossiers
and multi-tiered vetting before a decision by the Medical Devices Board, which was cumbersome and resulted in
significant processing delays.
To eliminate these bottlenecks, DRAP launched an end-to-end Online Registration and Licensing System,
inaugurated by the Prime Minister in July 2025. This digital platform ensures:
i. Online application submission and real-time tracking for transparency.
ii. Digital issuance of deficiency letters and registration certificates
iii. Automated workflows that eliminate human- induced delays.
(b) Under this digital platform, registration is now granted within an average of 22.30 working days,
provided all technical requirements are met by the applicant.
There is zero pendency under the new digital system, as applications are processed within an average of 22.30
working days. The system features an automated 'stop-the-clock' mechanism that pauses the countdown once a
deficiency is communicated to a firm, ensuring the processing timeline reflects only the time taken by the Authority.
However, regarding the manually submitted applications, DRAP has successfully cleared thousands of
applications, and currently only 800 applications now remain. These are typically pending due to factors beyond the

Authority’s control, primarily for the provision of critical international certifications or mandatory technical data
required under MDR, 2017.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Water Resource be pleased to state what steps are being taken by the
Government to strengthen Pakistan’s own water storage and management capacity in response to potential
upstream developments by India?
questions.reply:
 WAPDA maintains continuous real-time monitoring of river flows and streams including transboundary
flows entering from Indian illegally occupied Jammu & Kashmir (IIOJK) to Pakistan, reservoir levels, and
rainfall through an expanded hydrometeorological and telemetry network. This enables timely assessment of
upstream activities and supports evidence-based operational decisions.
 Reservoir operations at Tarbela, Mangla, and Chashma are carried out as per IRSA Indents and in
accordance with approved rules to ensure optimal regulation of flows, flood mitigation, and efficient water
distribution.
 In response to potential upstream developments by India, Govt. of Pakistan is taking several measures to
strengthen water management capacity through institutional, technical, and operational improvements. The
Government has also enhanced inter-agency coordination mechanisms among WAPDA, Federal Flood
Commission, Pakistan Commissioner for Indus Waters, Provincial Irrigation Departments, and Pakistan
Meteorological Department. These institutions share data regularly to improve flood forecasting, risk
assessment, and contingency planning.
 Moreover, established flood early warning systems are used to promptly communicate anticipated high flows
or emergency releases to downstream authorities, thereby strengthening preparedness and response capacity.
Collectively, these measures enhance Pakistan’s institutional readiness, technical monitoring capability, and
overall water governance framework in the context of transboundary water challenges.
 Following India’s unilateral and unlawful act of holding the Treaty in abeyance, Pakistan is closely
monitoring Indian activities affecting flows of rivers from IIOJK. Among these, Chenab River is most
vulnerable, as India can manipulate its waters through upstream developments.
 To address the situation, WAPDA has planned Chiniot Dam Project designed with a storage capacity of 1
MAF. PC-I of project is in a process of approval.
 WAPDA is also planning 03 additional storages namely Wazirabad, Midh Ranjha and Shah Jiwana to
regulate the flows of Chenab River.
 These 04 proposed storages (4.5 MAF) will enable effective regulation of Chenab River and serve to
counteract potential Indian interventions on its flows.
 To address Pakistan's growing water and energy needs, WAPDA is executing several mega-projects across
the Indus Basin to bolster the national water storage capacity. This strategic expansion is anchored by the
Diamer Basha Dam on Indus River, a project of existential importance that will provide a massive 6.4 MAF
live storage, acting as a "backstop" to the aging Tarbela reservoir. Downstream from this, the Dasu
Hydropower Project (also on the Indus) leverages the river’s high head for massive energy yields.
Simultaneously, the Mohmand Dam on the Swat River, having 0.676 MAF live storage is being developed as
a critical flood-mitigation and food-security asset for the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
WAPDA has also identified Dudhnial Multipurpose Project located on Neelum River in Azad Jammu &
Kashmir having 1 MAF storage capacity and aims to generate 960 MW of electricity.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Water Resources be pleased to state:
a) Why the Akram Wah canal faces “serious water shortages” and cannot supply farmers when most
needed, despite WAPDA initiating the Akram Wah Re-lining Project with a Rs 2.5 billion PSDP allocation to
prevent seepage losses estimated at 35-40% of water flow;
b) whether the project, aiming to reline 58 kilometers to serve 20,000 acres, was scheduled for completion
by June, 2025 but faces delays due to land acquisition disputes and contractor performance issues; and
c) what specific timeline exists for completion; and
d) what monitoring mechanism ensures the Rs 2.5 billion investment translates into measurable of above
water savings rather than leaving farmers without irrigation during critical sowing windows?
questions.reply:
(a) It is clarified at the outset, as
apprised by WAPDA, that Akram Wah canal does not fall under the jurisdiction of WAPDA, therefore the question
does not pertain to WAPDA. The Ministry of Water Resources accordingly obtained reply from Irrigation
Department, Government of Sindh according to which the design discharge of Akram Wah is 3,714 cusecs.
However, the existing concrete and brick lining is in very poor condition, with many sections having collapsed into
the channel, creating obstructions to the flow. As a result, the carrying capacity of Akram Wah has been reduced to
2,400 cusecs. It is clarified that Irrigation Department, the Government of Sindh, under the Sindh Water &
Agriculture Transformation (SWAT) Project (Irrigation Component), has planned to undertake the “Rehabilitation of
Akram Wah Works.” Currently, the project is in the procurement stage and is scheduled for completion in 3 years’
time.
(b) The scope of work includes relining the canal from RD 0 to RD 193, as well as the replacement of all
cross regulators, the head regulator, and other hydraulic structures. The project’s development objectives are to
increase agricultural water productivity and improve water resource management within a command area of 488,000
acres. The project is also expected to boost Sindh’s rural economy and address water-related environmental
degradation.
(c) The Procurement Process of “Rehabilitation Work of Akram Wah” is in Progress. The contract award is
targeted for mid-May 2026. The project is expected to be completed in 3 years.
(d) The project will be monitored and supervised by Project Implementation Consultants (PIC). Furthermore,
a multilayered, comprehensive monitoring and evaluation mechanism will also be carried out by Sindh Irrigation &
Drainage Authority (SIDA), Planning & Development Department (P&D) Government of Sindh through Project
Coordination & Monitoring Unit (PCMU), and the World Bank during project implementation under the Sindh
Water & Agriculture Transformation (SWAT). Project to ensure transparency, efficiency, and the achievement of
