questions.question:
Will the Minister for Information Technology and
Telecommunication be pleased to state:

(a) whether the Government is aware of the increasing
circulation of blasphemous, obscene and phonographic
content on social media platforms specially on TIKTOK in
Pakistan;

(b) whether existing monitoring, filtering and regulatory
mechanisms, including those of PTA and other implementing
agencies, have not been functioning effectively;

(c) whether it is a fact that the concerned authorities largely rely
on public complaints for action and are not performing a
proactive monitoring and enforcement role, if so, the reasons
therefor;

(d) the steps taken so far to block, remove and prevent such
unlawful content;

(e) whether the Government proposes corrective measures to
strengthen proactive monitoring, inter-agency coordination
and enforcement mechanism; and

(f) whether action will be taken to fix responsibility and hold
individuals and the platforms accountable for dissemination
of such content?
questions.reply:
(a) Measures taken by the Federal
Government and NCCIA to Curb Blasphemous, Obscene, and
Pornographic Content on Social Media (TikTok). The federal
government’s response to the proliferation of unlawful online content,
specifically on TikTok. The Government is fully aware of the increasing
circulation of blasphemous and pornographic material, which poses a
direct challenge to the moral and religious values of Pakistan. Through the
Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016, the state is utilizing a
multi-agency approach involving the NCCIA and the Pakistan
Telecommunication Authority (PTA) to monitor, block, and prosecute
offenders.

REGULATORY ACTION CONTENT REMOVAL

The NCCIA has identified and reported the following URLs for
immediate blocking:

x Blasphemous Content: 600+ URLs.

x Modesty of Natural Persons: 426 URLs.

x Offenses Against Dignity: 1,695 URLs.

ENFORCEMENT CRIME STATISTICS (2025)

The NCCIA remains actively engaged in investigating individuals
involved in the creation and dissemination of illegal content. The
following data represents the enforcement landscape for the year 2025:

53

SPECIAL REPORT: BLASPHEMY ENFORCEMENT

A dedicated focus on blasphemous content has yielded the
following legal outcomes for 2025:

x Complaints Received: 435.

x Enquiries Registered: 98.

x FIRs/Cases Registered: 42.

x Arrests Made: 73 individuals.

Legal Success: 3 Convictions and 1 Acquittal

(b) PTA has established regulatory mechanisms in accordance
with its mandate under PECA 2016 and relevant rules. These mechanisms
have resulted in the blocking and removal of a significant volume of
unlawful online content. PTA has processed more than 1.5 million
unlawful URLs for blocking through proactive and complaint-based
reporting. Apart from that, 6.5 million pornographic domains are also
blocked through WMS system installed by PTA. However, the evolving
nature, and huge volume of content being uploaded on the internet every
minute pose regulatory challenges, which are being addressed by the
Authority through continuous upgradation of resources.

(c) PTA employs a hybrid approach comprising public
complaints, coordination with other government stakeholders, proactive
methods, and consumer awareness. Public reporting serves as an important
mechanism due to the vast volume of objectionable online content
reported through PTA’s various complaint channels. As provided above,

54
significantly more content i.e. above 6.5 million URLs are removed
through proactive enforcement.

(d) PTA has taken multiple steps, including:

x Establishment of dedicated government reporting channels
with all major social media platforms and regular reporting of
unlawful online content.

x Deployment of WMS system to block entire HTTPS websites.

x Regular engagements and consultation sessions with social
media platforms for compliance with local laws.

x Training of all government stakeholders to report unlawful
online content to PTA as per their respective domains and
scope of work.

x Coordination with law enforcement agencies through an
efficient online portal for reporting content involving serious
offences.

x Comprehensive awareness campaigns for the general public
to encourage safe, responsible use of the Internet, and
enhance digital literacy in collaboration with local and
international entities such as Meta, TikTok, UNICEF, HEC,
etc.

(e) PTA is continuously undertaking measures to further
strengthen proactive mechanisms, enhance inter-agency coordination, and
improve technical capacity. These include capacity building, joint
consultation sessions, and engagement with platforms to ensure
compliance.

(f) Under section 29 of the PECA Amendments 2025, the
National Cyber Crime Agency (NCCIA) has been mandated to investigate
and take action against individuals involved in committing offenses under
PECA. However, as far as the accountability of platforms is concerned,
there is currently no criminal or civil liability upon the platform, but the
platforms are obligated under Rules 2021 to take action against the content
that is violative of the local laws of Pakistan.

55

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Information Technology and
Telecommunication be pleased to state:

(a) the steps taken by the Government during the last three years
to improve information technology and telecommunication
infrastructure in District Gujrat;

(b) whether any projects relating to broadband expansion, fiber
optic connectivity, 4G/5G services, public Wi-Fi facilities,
software technology parks, e-Rozgar centres, or digital skill
development initiatives have been launched or are under
consideration in District Gujrat;

(c) if so, the details thereof, including allocation of funds,
timelines and current status;

strengthening IT and telecommunication infrastructure in the
said district have been provided; if so, the details thereof;

(e) the challenges faced in expanding reliable internet and
telecommunication services in District Gujrat particularly in
rural and underserved areas; and

(f) the future roadmap and proposed projects, if any, to further
enhance digital connectivity and IT infrastructure in District
Gujrat?
questions.reply:
(a) Regarding cellular mobile services
availability and expansion in Distt. Gujrat, it is apprised that Cellular
Mobile Operators (CMOs) have established robust Telecom infrastructure
in Distt Gujrat. Details of sites supporting voice and data services installed
by the operators in last 3x years are as under:

a. Licensing of FLL and CVAS Operators

i. PTA has granted and renewed multiple Fixed Local Loop
(FLL) licenses for the Gujranwala Telecom Region (GTR),
which includes District Gujrat.

ii. There are Twenty-seven (27) FLL licensees in GTR, out of
these, Ten (10) FLL licenses were granted and Four (4) were
renewed during 2023~2025.

b. Introduction of District Level Class License

i. PTA has commenced the grant of Class Licenses for
Provision of Internet Services at the District Level from 1st
January, 2026.

65
ii. The initiative is expected to encourage local entrepreneurship
and enable small and medium-sized enterprises to serve
District Gujrat, particularly in underserved tehsils and rural
areas currently not commercially viable for larger operators.

iii. Key features of the License includes:

(1). Jurisdiction: Single district per license; 10-year term
(renewable)

(2). Initial License Fee of PKR 300,000 plus Annual
License Fee of PKR 100,000 (with 10% annual
increment)

(3). Rollout obligation: Services to commence within 1
year; minimum 100 broadband connections within 1 year
of commencement

iv. Details of the District Level Class License are enclosed as
Annexure-A.

66

67
(b) GoP and PTA have undertaken a range of policy and
regulatory measures to support broadband expansion and provide robust
Telecom Infrastructure foundation.

Multiple nationwide initiatives such as, Right of Way (ROW)
facilitation, introduction of new technologies (5G), VoWiFi enablement,
enhanced Quality of Service (QoS) and Infrastructure sharing framework
are in place which continue to support enhancement of digital connectivity
and IT infrastructure in Distt. Gujrat.

In terms of broadband expansion and 4G/5G services, Cellular
Mobile Operators (CMOs) are mandated under their newly issued licenses
to progressively expand network coverage and capacity across the country.
Furthermore, 5G rollout will deliver higher data speeds, lower latency, and
improved reliability, enabling advanced services such as loT, smart cities,
e-health, and e-education, and supporting overall digital transformation
and economic growth in Pakistan.

(c) The licenses issued after recent NGMS/5G spectrum auction
includes enhanced targets for rollout and QoS obligations. It obligates
CMOs to deploy at least 1,000 4G/5G sites per year. 4G sites shall be
proportionately distributed between urban and rural areas in each province
whereas 5G rollout prioritizes Federal and Provincial capitals, including
Islamabad/Rawalpindi, Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar, and Quetta, in the first
phase, with subsequent expansion to other major cities. CMOs are in
process of procuring/ import of equipment to establish new 4G/5G sites
and a visible enhancement in coverage/QoS is expected in next 4 to 6
months.

New 4G sites will enhance network performance and QoS by
increasing capacity and reducing congestion.

(d) The necessary IT and telecommunication infrastructure
required for provision of telecom services is already in place and
operational. Cellular Mobile Operators (CMOS) have deployed requisite
network infrastructure, including base stations, transmission systems, and
supporting facilities, to ensure service availability and continuity.
However, the maintenance of such infrastructure is a continuous and
ongoing process and CMOs are responsible for regular maintenance,
optimization, and upgrades of their networks to ensure consistent quality
of service and to cater growing user demands.

68
Furthermore, PTA has issued NGMS/5G license on 19th March
2026 and introduction of 5G service is underway nationwide and will be
extended to District Gujrat in due course.

(e) CHALLENGES FACED:-

a. Unreliable and intermittent electricity supply in rural areas
adversely affects the uptime.

b. Frequent OFC cuts caused by road construction, unauthorized
digging, and vandalism result in service disruptions.

c. Sparse population density and lower Average Revenue Per
User (ARPU) in rural areas make commercial operations
financially challenging for private operators.

(f) Future roadmap for cellular services expansion:

As per the recently issued licenses, CMOs are required to deploy at
least 1,000 4G/5G sites per year, and implementation of 5G across
Pakistan will be carried out in following four phases:

i. Phase 1 (2026-2028): 5G Launch in Federal and Provincial
capitals i.e Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Karachi, Lahore,
Peshawar, and Quetta.

ii. Phase 2 (2028-2030): 5G expansion to 10 x additional cities
(at least 2x cities from each province).

iii. Phase 3 (2030-2032): Further 5G rollout in 10 x additional
cities (at least 2 x cities from each province).

iv. Phase 4 (2032-2035): 5G rollout in 15 x additional cities (at
least 2 x cities from each province).

Furthermore, enhanced Quality of Service (QoS) thresholds are
also incorporated in said licenses, data rate for 4G has been enhanced from
4 Mbps to 20 Mbps, with a further increase to 50 Mbps in a phased
manner. For 5G, data rate of 50 Mbps has been introduced, with an end-
state target of 100 Mbps in phased manner to ensure significantly
improved network performance and user experience.

(Annexures have been placed in the National Assembly Library).

9001:2015 certified Division since 2017. As per requirements of ISO
9001: 2015 Standard, a Quality Management System is in place in
Establishment Division. Accordingly, the functions, job-descriptions of

6
officers/officials and processes/procedures (SOPs) of Establishment
Division have been documented and standardized in line with the
Establishment Division’s functions as per Rules of Business, 1973. As
such, the requirements of ISO 9001: 2015 Standard are used as a
benchmark for evaluating the performance of Establishment Division.
Furthermore, in compliance of the Federal Cabinet Decision made in its
meeting held on 16th July, 2025, Key Performance Indicators are being
developed for the Establishment Division and after approval of the Prime
Minister, the same will be implemented in Establishment Division
onwards (Annex).

(b) To monitor the performance of Establishment Division, as per
requirements of ISO 9001: 2015 Standard, external auditors of
Certification Body conduct Annual Surveillance (3rd party) audit. Based
on the findings of External Auditors, the identified observations, non-
conformities etc. are communicated to the respective Wings of
Establishment Division for rectification. Besides, each year internal audits
(Wing wise) of Establishment Division are also conducted wherein
deficiencies in the performance vis-a-vis workplace environment are
identified and addressed. Furthermore, a Management Review Committee,
constituted under the Chair of Establishment Secretary, also annually
reviews the performance of Establishment Division, including external
surveillance/ certification audit observations, internal audit findings,
annual Clients Satisfaction Survey Report and accordingly decisions are
made for continual improvement in the performance of Establishment
Division.

(Annexure has been placed in the National Assembly Library).

questions.question:
Will the Minister In-charge of the Prime Minister’s Office be
pleased to state:

(a) whether it is a fact that NDMA did not provide on time
accurate assessment of losses and a comprehensive
rehabilitation strategy after several disasters;

(b) if so, the reasons for such delay;

(c) whether any complaints have been received regarding the
untimely disbursement of funds allocated for the
rehabilitation of the affected areas; and

(d) the measures adopted by the government to redress such
complaints?
questions.reply:
(a) 1. The
factual position in the disaster management framework of Pakistan is that
the District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs)/ District
Administration and Provincial Disaster Management Authorities
(PDMAs) act as the first and second tier responders respectively. NDMA
primarily functions as a Federal coordinating and policy-formulating
body. During the monsoon season and other disaster situations, NDMA
regularly issues Daily Situation Reports (SITREPs) based on information
received from provinces and relevant stakeholders. These reports provide
consolidated updates on losses and damages as well as response measures,
including rescue operations, establishment of relief and medical camps
and relief assistance provided to the affected population.

2. In order to enhance transparency and timely dissemination of
disaster information, NDMA has also developed a disaster reporting
dashboard. The key features of the dashboard include:-

a. Depiction of number of deaths and injuries.

b. Cause of death and injuries.

c. Gender-stgregated data.

d. Details of losses (damaged houses, roads, and other
infrastructure).

e. Provincial and district-wise breakdown of data.

f. Information on rescue and evacuation operations.

g. Relief assistance provided.

h. Self-explanatory mapping and visualization of disaster
impacts.

8
3. Furthermore, NDMA compiles and publishes post-disaster
reports for major national-level events, such as post-monsoon reports,
seasonal reports and incident reports, which provide a comprehensive
overview of disaster impacts and response measures. However, in the case
of large-scale disasters, such as the floods of 2022 and 2025, the Ministry
of Planning, Development Special Initiatives (MoPD	SI) assumes the
lead role in conducting detailed damage and needs assessments and in
formulating recovery and rehabilitation frameworks (4RF) in coordination
with relevant stakeholders. Accordingly, detailed data regarding
comprehensive rehabilitation strategies may be obtained from the said
Ministry.

Following the 2022 floods, the Government of Pakistan undertook
a comprehensive Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) in
collaboration with provincial govemments and international development
partners. The PDNA provided detailed and evidence-based estimates of
damages, losses, and recovery needs across all major sectors of the
economy. Based on the findings of the PDNA, the Resilient Recovery,
Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Framework (4RF) was developed under
the leadership of the Ministry of Planning, Development Special
Initiatives (MoPD	SI) to guide coordinated recovery, rehabilitation and
reconstruction efforts across affected areas. Similarly, following the 2025
monsoon floods, the Government conducted a Preliminary Assessment of
Flood Damages in the Economy of Pakistan, which has been published on
the website of the Planning Commission. To further enhance accuracy and
strengthen future preparedness, the Government is currently undertaking a
damage validation and lessons learned exercise in collaboration with
provincial governments and development partners. This exercise aims to
review and validate assessment findings, identify systemic gaps, and
develop a forward-looking roadmap for a more resilient and risk-informed
disaster management system.

(b) No delay reported. Progress on recovery rehabilitation
projects under the umbrella of 4RF (Monsoon 2022; may be sought from
MoPD	SI).

No delay has been reported in the conduct of damage
assessments and preparation of recovery planning.

9
(c) No delay reported. Progress on recovery rehabilitation
projects under the umbrella of 4RF (Monsoon 2022; may be sought from
MoPD	SI).

No complaints have been reported to MoPDSI regarding the non-
timely disbursement of allocated funds for rehabilitation of affected areas.

(d) Any complain received at NDMA; is immediately responded
and respective DDMA/PDMA or federal resources/ departments are
conveyed for necessary action to be followed up later.

Not applicable in view of reply at part (c)

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Poverty Alleviation and Social Safety be
pleased to state what is the process for verification of the
beneficiaries of Benazir Income Support Program or Social Safety
net?
questions.reply:
The beneficiaries of Benazir Income Support Program
(BISP)’s Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) /Conditional Cash
Transfers (CCT) programmes are identified through National Socio
Economic Registry (NSER) survey using a scientific assessment
methodology at the Tehsil level based on real-time household data
including CNIC, family composition (B-Forms) and socio-economic
variables.

The eligibility is determined on the basis of Proxy Means Test
(PMT) score, which measures a household’s welfare status on a scale
between 0-100. The PMT is globally recognized and reliable tool with
high predictive accuracy for assessing household living standards. The
PMT cut-off score for eligibility is determined by the BISP Board based
on available fiscal space. Currently, a PMT score of 32 is applied as the
general eligibility threshold. For households with persons with disabilities,
the cut-off score is 37. Furthermore, transgender individuals registered
with NADRA under the recognized gender category and surveyed through
NSER are included in the programme without any PMT score restriction.

In addition, surveyed households are cross-verified for profiling
filters against various external Government of Pakistan administrative
databases (e.g., self / spouse government employee, self / spouse

11
pensioner, self /spouse registration in ATL (Active Taxpayers List) or
Sales Tax, etc.) to ensure that only genuinely vulnerable households are
enrolled in the programme.

For disbursement of cash assistance to BISP beneficiaries, bank
accounts of each beneficiary are opened by BISP partner banks after
internal screening and KYC verification from NADRA. Activation of
Bank accounts and withdrawal of cash assistance is made after live
biometric verification of beneficiaries through NADRA.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Industries and Production be pleased to state:

(a) what plan is under consideration of the Government to revive
industrial growth and investment in the country as industrial sector
is facing severe crisis due to high energy tariffs; and

(b) whether there is a proposal to abolish cross subsidies imposed on
industry and reduce the policy rate to single digit, curing interest
rates initially to 9 percent and then to 7 percent to revive industrial
growth and investment besides addressing the issue of expensive
electricity?
questions.reply:
(a) It is submitted that matters
relating to determination of energy tariffs fall within the domain of the Ministry
of Energy (Power Division). However, MOIP/ Engineering Development Board
(EDB) supports rationalization of energy tariffs for the industrial sector, as
competitive energy pricing is essential for sustaining industrial growth and
attracting investment.

Furthermore, recent Large-Scale Manufacturing indicators reflect signs
of stabilization and recovery in key sectors, indicating improved capacity
utilization and industrial growth. Details are placed at Annex A.

EDB/MoIP approach to reviving industrial growth is focused on
maintaining a stable and investment friendly policy environment. In this regard,
EDB/MoIP is implementing targeted sectoral policies including the Automotive
Industry Development and Export Policy 2021-2026, the Mobile Device
Manufacturing Policy and the New Energy Vehicle Policy 2025-2030, which
provide structured incentives such as tariff rationalization, localization support,
technology upgradation and facilitation of new investment.

2
(b) It is submitted that the policy rate is determined by the State Bank
of Pakistan, while fiscal policy matters fall under the Ministry of Finance.
Electricity tariffs and cross subsidies are within the jurisdiction of the Ministry of
Energy (Power Division).

No specific proposal in this regard is under consideration in the
Engineering Development Board. However, MoIP/ EDB supports measures that
reduce cost of capital and energy to promote industrial growth.

(Annexure has been placed in the National Assembly Library). Click here for annexure

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and
Coordination be pleased to state:

(a) what is the current timeline for the full integration of Electronic
Medical Records (EMR) across all tertiary care hospitals in the
capital/province;

(b) how is Ministry addressing the digital literacy gap among existing
staff; and

(c) what measures are being adopted to ensure that patients in remote
areas with limited internet connectivity are not excluded from
digital wallets services?
questions.reply:
(a) The Ministry of NHR&C has conceived a full-
fledged project namely Electronic Universal Electronic Medical Record (e-UMR)
aims to be executed under PSDP. The project shall provide; a smart software
with AI features, technical assistance and interoperability of the Health
Management Information Systems (HMIS) of public sector tertiary care hospital
in ICT in the first phase and then expanding the connectivity to the private sector
hospitals presently on the panel of Prime Minister Sehat Sahulat Programme. In
the second phase, the project shall be extended to the provinces and such tertiary
care hospitals and clinics where maturity level of their respective Management
Information Systems are progressed well as per the standards in due course of
time. The first phase is expected to be completed in 12 months, while the
Ministry of NHSR&C shall complete the procurement process of technical
consultant of the project by June, 2026. The Ministry of NHSR&C has already
take initiative of holding inter Ministerial conference inviting Ministers from
Provinces to gather their support and sharing of data for development of
respective data bases required in maintaining e-UMR. The project is expected to
be completed all across Pakistan by December, 2028.

(b) The need for digital governance could hardly be over emphasized.
In this connection, the Ministry of NHSR&C is fully cognizant of fact that the
human resource serving at various positions in the Ministry must undergo IT-
related trainings enabling them to respond effectively in the evolving digital
governance. In the last 12 month, capacity building programme under taking of
E-office and digital governance, helped desk and technical support, training of
various IT software and exposure to digital monitoring evaluation of different
projects.
List of the training is attached for ready reference.

(c) For the fist time in the history of National Health Services, this
Ministry has launched a Telemedicine Pilot Project that aims to provide primary
health care services from 06 BHUs in Islamabad and 04 Federal Government
Dispensaries in Karachi. The patient living in far-flung areas in Islamabad can
now access selected Basic Health Units in Islamabad where state-of-the-art
internet connectivity has been provided. With the help of an NGO-Sehat Kahani,
the Ministry has ensured that online Medical Doctors /General Physicians and
Consultants are available at these BHUs turned Telemedicine Centers especially
for people residing in remote areas of Islamabad. The Ministry, however, aims to
launched a dedicated telemedicine project under PSDP which has already been
approved by CDWP in January, 2026. The lesson learnt from aforesaid pilot
project shall be incorporated in the main telemedicine project under PSDP and

4
upon its successful completion, with in a period of next 18 months, the
telemedicine facilities shall be available for other rural areas of the country as
well. On the other hand, Ministry is also actively engaged with the other
International Financial Institutions (IFIs) for developing a complete e-health road
map, along with an investment plan, having a synergetic contribution from
telecommunication companies and internet service providers as well.

(Annexure has been placed in the National Assembly Library).Click here for annexure

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Housing and Works be pleased to state:

(a) details of officers/officials who have been allotted residential plots
by Federal Government Employees Housing Authority, who
have already been allotted in other Federal or Provincial Housing
Schemes; and

(b) what are the relevant rules and reasons thereof?
questions.reply:
(a)
The Federal Government Employees Housing Authority allots residential plots to
only those officers / officials who have not been allotted plots by CDA or any
other Government controlled Agency in Federal Capital. Furthermore, the
allotments in Private and Provincial Housing Schemes are exempted and no
record of such allotments are maintained by the FGEHA. Hence, reply may be
treated as ‘NIL’.

(b) As per allotment policy duly approved by the Executive Committee
of FGEHA, a Federal Government Employees who have been already allotted a
plot by CDA or any other Government controlled Agency in Federal Capital is
non-eligible for allotment though FGEHA. However, allotment through Private
and Provincial Housing Schemes do not affect the eligibility of Federal
Government employees and they are allotted plots by FGEHA, as per allotment
policy.

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and
Coordination be pleased to state:

(a) how many Private Hospitals, Clinics are operating in Islamabad,
details of their names, addresses and the authority from whom they
get permission of operating such kind of hospitals;

(b) whether it is a fact that some hospitals located in Islamabad do not
have permission from relevant office/Ministry;

(c) whether it is also a fact that most of these hospitals do not
have proper arrangements to dispose of the human waste; and

(d) what action has been taken against these hospitals who does not
have proper arrangements to dispose of the human waste?
questions.reply:
(a) Details of Health Care Establishments (HCE’s) are
as under:

Total HCE’s registered: 2001,

That it is an extensive list, Names and other details of all Healthcare
establishments (HCE’s) are available at IHRA’s website on the following link,
https://ihra.gov.pk/provisionally-registered-hces/.

Permission for operation of all such HCE’s is granted by the Islamabad
Healthcare Regulatory Authority (IHRA) under IHR Act 2018.

(b) IHRA has catered maximum number of HCE’s under regulatory
framework and had them registered, after fulfilling codal formalities under the
law. Furthermore, there are 42 enforcement ad 24 inspection teams in field for
the whole month which operates against all such HCE’s, ensure their registration
which are not yet registered with IHRA as well as take necessary action against
quacks. Statistics of actions against such HCE’s in last 02 months is attached at
Annex- A.

(c) IHRA has collaborated with the Pak Environmental Protection
Agency (EPA) to monitor the entire medical waste management process in ICT.
This included joint inspections of various hospitals to ensure proper waste
collection, segregation, transportation, and disposal practices were being
followed.

The IHRA has launched an electronic portal for entering medical waste
data on its website. This system aims to streamline data collection, enhance
transparency, and facilitate better tracking and management of medical waste
from both hospitals and waste management companies in ICT.

Meeting of public and private healthcare establishments and waste
management companies operating in ICT was called on 25th June 2024 to
discuss the implementation regarding infectious waste management in ICT.

6
On March 11th, 2025, IHRA convened a review meeting with major
tertiary healthcare facilities from both the public and private sectors and waste
management companies. The purpose of the meeting was to assess the progress
made concerning the PM’s directives and the adherence to IHRA standards for
hospital waste management.

Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority (IHRA) has developed
standards for disposal of infectious waste by HCEs in ICT and implementing
these standards while registration and licensing of HCES. IHRA ensures that any
registered entity or establishment will follow its standards for disposal of
infectious waste.

IHRA has brought all stakeholders (like private waste management
companies, public and private sector hospitals & EPA) on one platform to
monitor the disposal of medical waste as per WHO guidelines.

IHRA has launched an INFECTIOUS WASTE MANAGEMENT
PORTAL on the IHRA website: ihra.gov.pk/waste-management-hce, which is a
centralized system to store and manage all data related to medical waste
management.

(d) IHRA has focused its attention to 12 tertiary care hospitals of ICT
that are producing more than 80% of infectious waste.

IHRA is ensuring that these hospitals regularly upload their data
meanwhile IHRA is also following with smaller healthcare facilities.

IHRA has issued 499 notices in the form of letters to non-compliant
healthcare facilities that are not reporting their medical waste information on
electronic monitoring system in ICT.

Majority of the HCE sealed / suspended / issued notice [referred in
Annex- B] pertaining to non compliance of improper mechanism of waste
management and non following of IPC guidelines.

IHRA inspection teams has initiated zone wise inspections across ICT to
monitor compliance of all healthcare establishments ensuring their medical waste
is either incinerated at their own site or handed over to private incineration
companies for proper disposal.

IHRA inspection teams, during field visits, focused on raising awareness
among HCEs staff regarding protocols for disposal of infectious waste and
registered waste management companies.

7

questions.ministry: National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination
questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and
Coordination be pleased to state:

(a) what is the current number of registered HIV/AIDS patients in
Pakistan with a province-wise and region-wise breakdown of
said cases;

(b) whether UNAIDS has expressed any reservations regarding the
Government’s reporting; and

(c) what strategy has been adopted for the prevention, awareness,
diagnosis, treatment, funding and control of the spread of
HIV/AIDS in the country?
questions.reply:
(a) As per the latest available data from the National
AIDS Control Programme, a total of approximately 84,421 people are registered
as living with HIV in Pakistan. A detailed province-wise and region-wise
breakdown is maintained and regularly updated by the program. The distribution
indicates that the highest number of reported cases are from Punjab and Sindh,
followed by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory.
A comprehensive breakdown is placed at Annex-I.

(b) UNAIDS maintains close collaboration with the Government of
Pakistan and supports the national HIV response through technical assistance and

8
strategic guidance. While periodic discussions are held to further strengthen
surveillance, estimation and reporting mechanisms, no formal reservations have
been expressed. Continuous efforts are underway to align national reporting with
international standards and improve data quality.

(c) The Government has adopted a comprehensive, multi-sectoral
strategy for the prevention and control of HIV/AIDS, which includes:

 Prevention & Awareness: Targeted awareness campaigns,
particularly among key populations, community engagement, and
for young students & religious leaders.

 Diagnosis: Expansion of HIV testing services, including facility-
based and community-based testing, to ensure early detection.

 Treatment: Free antiretroviral therapy (ART) is being provided
through a network of 98 treatment centers across the country. In
addition, the National HIV Lost to Follow-Up Strategy has been
implemented to strengthen retention of people living with HIV in
care and ensure continuity of treatment. Provincial coordination has
been sought for this strategy.

 Surveillance: Strengthening of integrated biological and behavioral
surveillance systems to monitor trends.

 Funding: Mobilization of domestic and international resources,
including support from development partners.

 Control Measures: Harm reduction programs, safe blood
transfusion practices, and infection prevention and control measures
in healthcare settings. The letters have been written to all provincial
healthcare commissions and IHRA for implementing Infection
Prevention and Control (IPC) measures.

The Government remains fully committed to controlling the spread of
HIV/AIDS and ensuring access to prevention, treatment, and care services for all
affected populations.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Railways be pleased to state:

(a) the year wise volume and value of freight handled by Pakistan
Railways during the last five years, along with the annual increase
or decrease observed therein;

(b) whether it is a fact that freight wagons were detached from various
trains in recent months, including the Thal Express; if so, the
reasons and details thereof;

(c) whether such incidents do not reflect negatively on the operational
efficiency and profitability of Pakistan Railways;

(d) what steps are being taken to ensure uninterrupted freight
movement, eliminate such inefficiencies, and enhance freight
handling capacity; and

(e) what strategies are put in place to access untapped freight
potential, improve infrastructure, attract new logistics business,
and increase Pakistan Railways market share in national freight
transport?
questions.reply:
(a) Pakistan
Railways’ earnings during the last five years are as under:-

Year Freight Earning
(Rs. in Million)
Tonnes Carried
(in Millions)
Increase/Decrease
2020-21 20,478 8.213
2021-22 23,001 8.098 -115
2022-23 17,495 5.748 -2350
2023-24 28,009 7.854 2106
2024-25 31,624 7.753 -101

(b) Thal Express is a passenger train running with passenger coaches,
whereas, freight trains consist of freight wagons. Only those coaches, wagons,
brake vans, and luggage vans are withdrawn from trains that are operationally not
fit for safe train operations or are commercially non-viable. These are reattached
after maintenance and availability.

Thal Express 129DN/130UP is plying between Rawalpindi and Multan
with 5 economy coaches and one power plant. On average, 370 passengers per
day are traveling in this train (in the last 3 months), which is 75% of its seating
capacity.

(c) The incidents of detachment of coaches from trains are a temporary
phenomenon only to ensure operational efficiency as well as the safety of train
operation. The requisite safety standards and the availability of cargo and
passengers are considered while planning train composition and operation.
Periodic traffic volume assessment is also carried out, and coaches are
increased/decreased as per traffic demand.

(d) Pakistan Railways has initiated the following measures to further
improve the freight operations, some steps are listed below.

1. For the expansion of the freight operations, the Thar coal project of
rail connectivity is under process.

2. 820 new high capacity freight wagons and 230 passenger coaches
are being inducted.

13
3. For regional connectivity, the Islamabad-Tehran-Istanbul train
service is planned to be resumed by the end of this year.

4. To improve safety and punctuality, E-inspections and Pakistan
Railways Accident Management System (PRAMS) are being
undertaken.

5. Two projects for immediate track safety works in the Sukkur
Division of the Pakistan Railways are being undertaken.

6. To enhance the role of the private sector, Pakistan Railways has
successfully auctioned two Cargo Trains operating between
Karachi-Lahore and Karachi-Multan-Faisalabad.

(e) Pakistan Railways is working on up gradation of its infrastructure
to increase its transport capacity by 5 times. Secondly, private sector is being
encouraged to invest in freight sector through track access and terminal
development. Special focus is also on regional transit traffic. In addition, through
digitization and improved governance, Pakistan Railways has planned to increase
its freight market share to 30% by 2035.

and

questions.reply:

present, the facility for purchasing railway tickets through bank cards is not
available at any railway station in the country. This is primarily due to the non-
availability of telecommunication (telco) services across Pakistan Railways
network, particularly on Main Line-1 (ML-1). Although provision of Point of
Sale (POS) machines has already been contracted under a Government-to-
Government (G2G) framework, the same could not be implemented due to these
constraints. Pakistan Railways has, however, initiated the Railway Advanced
Infrastructure Network project to provide high-speed broadband internet through
optical fiber at major stations, which will facilitate smooth implementation of
bank card payment systems.

(b) Consequently, this facility is not available at any station of Pakistan
Railways.

(c) Alternative digital payment mechanisms are available through the
RABTA (Railway Automated Booking and Travel Assistance) App as well as
mobile financial services such as JazzCash, Easypaisa, and UPaisa/Omni,
wherein payment gateways have been integrated. Ticket Vending Machines
(TVMs) have been installed at 57 major commercial stations for passenger
facilitation. It is expected that the facility for payment through bank cards will be
made available by the end of the current financial year.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Railways be pleased to state:

(a) whether it is a fact that railway tickets purchased through vouchers
are neither refundable nor allowed to be rescheduled to another
date under the existing ticketing policy of Pakistan Railways;

(b) if so, the rationale, policy basis and justification for imposing such
restrictions on passengers who purchase tickets through vouchers;

(c) whether the Government has conducted any review of the current
ticketing system to ensure that it is modern, transparent and
consumer friendly particularly with respect to refunds rescheduling
and ticket amendments;

(d) whether there is any proposal under consideration to modernize the
railways ticketing system including the introduction of flexible
refund and rescheduling policies similar to international best
practices; and

(e) what corrective or reform measures, if any are being adopted to
protect passengers rights, and

(f) what further steps are being taken to improve customer
convenience in the ticketing and reservation system of Pakistan
Railways?
questions.reply:
(a) Vouchers
are issued in lieu of concessions offered by Pakistan Railways. Each concessional
voucher carries a unique identification number which is entered into the
computerized reservation system to avail concession. Once a concession is
availed the same voucher number cannot be entered into reservation system to
secure another reservation. Hence there is no facility available for rescheduling
of tickets booked on vouchers. For rescheduling of tickets the passenger needs to
present a new concessional voucher.

However the tickets booked on vouchers can be refunded any time by the
ticket holders.

(b) The restriction is based on the following rationale:

 Accounting Controls: Vouchers are issued as a substitute for cash,
often under specific head of accounts (e.g., concessions). Allowing
rescheduling would create accounting discrepancies and potential
misuse.

20
 Prevention of Fraud: Vouchers are issued in controlled numbers.
Permitting amendments could lead to duplication, unauthorized
encashment, or misuse of government revenue instruments.

 Policy Consistency: The policy aligns with the principle that
vouchers are one-time instruments intended for a specific journey,
similar to non-transferable concessionary tickets.

(c) Yes. Pakistan Railways has transitioned from the legacy PRIMS
system to the RABTA system, which is a modern, web-based, and centralized
ticketing platform. This RABTA Reservation System has been acquired from a
reputable Chinese firm (M/S Easyway Innovation). This company is already
providing reservation and ticketing solutions to many International companies
and Railway Systems like in China, Hong Kong, Brazil, South Africa and Dubai
Metro. This RABTA Reservation System has been deployed in Pakistan
Railways on 05.05.2023 with the following user friendly salient features

 Real-time seat availability.

 Transparent online / e-ticketing.

 Development of RABTA APP for reservations.

 Development of APP for monitoring real time movement of trains
including intimation regarding expected time of arrival (ETA)

 Use of debit cards / credit cards, mobile wallets for reservation of
tickets by means of cash less transaction.

 Options of refunds and rescheduling of tickets readily available.

 Real time feed back and complaints options are also available on
the RABTA application for continuous improvements.

(d) As already discussed in the above para that a modern Advance
Reservation System has been introduced in Pakistan Railways on 05.05.2023.
Moreover, Pakistan Railways is actively working on upgrading the RABTA
system to introduce more flexible features to provide maximum convenience
/facilitation to the travelling public. Pakistan Railways is already providing
flexible refund and rescheduling.

 Time-slab based cancellation charges (lower charges for early
cancellations).

 Online rescheduling facility is also available.

21

 5% discount to all the passengers who reserve tickets 48 hours
before departure of trains.

(e) The RABTA system incorporates multiple safeguards, including:

 Standardize user friendly refund policy applied uniformly

 Digital record-keeping for transparency

 Centralized monitoring to prevent misuse

 Complaint redressal mechanisms

 Pakistan Railways is implementing the following initiatives under
the RABTA ecosystem:

 RABTA Mobile App: Launch of a user-friendly mobile application
for booking, cancellation, and rescheduling.

 Self-service kiosks: Installation of automated ticketing kiosks at
major Railway Stations.

 Integration with banking apps: Allowing ticket purchases and
refunds via JazzCash, Easypaisa, and major bank apps.

 Unified refund policy: Simplification of refund rules across cash,
card, and voucher categories with clear timelines.

 Dashboard for monitoring: Real-time monitoring of refund /
rescheduling requests at headquarters to ensure timely processing
and compliance with service standards.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Industries and Production be pleased to state:

(a) whether the Government has introduced any major industrial
support packages such as the Prime Minister’s Industries and
Farmers Package offering reduced electricity costs for industry to
enhance competitiveness and lower production costs;

(b) the sectors and regions prioritized under this package; and

(f)

(c) how these measures are expected to contribute for job creating
especially for youth within industrial and related supply chains?
questions.reply:
(a) Yes, the Government has
recently introduced an Incremental Consumption Package for both industrial and
agricultural consumers. The package is currently in effect and consumers have
already benefited from this initiative. Under the scheme, a discount of over Rs.
10 per unit is being provided on incremental consumption, which translates into
an approximate reduction of Rs. 2 per unit in overall electricity bills.

(b) The package has been extended to industrial and agricultural
consumers. All eligible consumers within these categories are able to avail
benefits of the scheme subject to the prescribed terms and conditions.

(c) Industrial consumers typically have scalable demand. With a clear
long-term pricing signal over a three-year horizon, industries are incentivized to
increase production by adding additional shifts or expanding operations in
response to the discounted tariff. This is expected to stimulate industrial activity
and generate employment opportunities across the value chain, including
manufacturing, logistics, and supporting services.

implementing the same?
questions.reply:
(a) The project titled “Up-gradation of Existing
Facilities of Hepatobiliary and Organ Transplant Centre at Pakistan
Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), Islamabad” was envisaged and
submitted for approval. The project was considered by the Central Development
Working Party (CDWP) in its meeting held on 24.05.2018 and was accorded
approval at a total cost of Rs. 603.94 million (without FEC). However, due to the
facts narrated in the second part of the reply, the same could not materialize.

In a bid to operationalize the existing facility, recruitment. for various
specialist positions was undertaken. Howeve the recruited two Specialists
subsequently resigned from their positions.

29
(b) Subsequent to the approval of the project, certain administrative
issues emerged regarding the reflection of the project in the PSDP. PIMS vide
letter No. F.109-1/2018 (OTC)/PIMS dated 10.07. 2018 (Annex-l) brought to the
notice of the then Capital Administration and Development Division (the
controlling Division of PIMS) that the project had been reflected in PSDP
2018-19 under a different title, i.e., “Upgradation of Existing Liver Transplant
Centre at PIMS,” with an allocation of Rs. 500.00 million, whereas the
approved PC-I bore a different title and cost. It was accordingly requested that
the project title in PSDP be corrected to align with the approved PC-I.

In response to PIMS’ request for floating of tenders dated 19.07.2018,
the then Capital Administration and Development Division vide O.M dated
01.08.2018 (Annex-II) intimated that the project was not reflected in the PSDP
2018-19 of the Division, therefore no tendering process could be initiated until
allocation of funds.

(a) whether the Government has introduced or is developing

Government, through the Ministry of Industries and Production (Mol&P) and its
executing arm SMEDA, is undertaking a wide range of coordinated policy,
financial, technical, and institutional measures to stimulate growth, increase
production, reduce the trade deficit and expand employment opportunities within
the SME sector. The key steps include:

30
1. Implementation of National SME Policy

2. Incentives for Women Entrepreneurs - Business Skill Development
Centre for Women, Digital Skills Training women-Inclusive
Women Entrepreneurship Policy & Action Plan, and Women
Enpreneurship Portal.

3. Matching Grants & Capital Support - 1000 Industrial Stitching Unit
Project

4. Productivity Support & Boosting Exports - Industry Support
Program, SME Certification, International Accreditation, & Quality
Improvement Program, and Export Assistance Program for SMEs,
and SME Sub-Contracting Program.

Credit Scoring initiative.

Centre (SIDC) Sialkot.

Portal

matching grants for industrial stitching units, youth can start manufacturing
ventures with reduced capital burden, while export assistance, certification
support, and subcontracting programs help them integrate into global value
chains and secure larger buyers. Productivity and industry support programs
enhance operational efficiency, quality standards, and energy management,
making young businesses more sustainable and globally competitive. Financial
literacy initiatives, credit scoring services, and dedicated facilitation desks
improve young entrepreneurs understanding of financing options and increase
their bankability Cluster-based common facilities, such as shared production and

31
testing centers reduce infrastructure costs and provide technical support.
Dedicated incentives for women and digital skills training promote inclusive
entrepreneurship, enabling young women to launch and scale tech-enabled
ventures. Climate resilience tools, carbon footprint calculators and green
productivity programs prepare youth-led enterprises for emerging sustainability
standards, while formalization support and simplified registration systems enable
them to access government schemes, legal protections, and institutional markets-
ultimately fostering innovation, job creation, and long-term enterprise growth
across the country.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Food Security and Research be
pleased to state:

(a) whether the Ministry has formulated any national food
traceability or inspection policy; and

(b) what steps have been taken by the Government to strengthen
quality checks for poultry and perishable items entering
urban food chains?
questions.reply:
(a) At present, the Ministry of National Food
Security and Research has not formulated comprehensive national food
traceability or integrated food inspection policy covering the entire food
chain from production to consumption. However, food safety, inspection,
and traceability functions are presently implemented through sector-
specific regulatory frameworks and provincial mechanisms following
constitutional devolution after 18th Amendment. The Ministry has
initiated institutional and regulatory reforms aimed at establishing a
harmonized national framework, including the establishment of the
National Agri-trade and Food Safety Authority (NAFSA), for
development of SPS-compliant inspection and certification systems.
Moreover, a five year PSDP program titled “National Program for Animal
Disease Surveillance, FMD and PPR Control, and Animal Track and
Traceability in Compliance with National and International Standards”,
with cost of PKR 7.350 billion, has also been approved. This program
aims to establish a National Animal Identification and Traceability
System for livestock and poultry building the foundation for traceability
of animal origin food products. The program will be implemented in
coordination with provincial livestock departments. Similarly, the
upcoming wheat policy 2026-30, beside other areas will focus on digital
traceability mechanisms. These measures are intended to progressively
support the development of an integrated national food traceability and
inspection system.

(b) Ministry of National Food Security and Research does not
exercise regulatory jurisdiction over routine quality control, inspection, or
enforcement relating to poultry meat, perishable food items, and retail
food safety. These responsibilities fall within the mandate of Provincial
Food Safety Authorities, established under respective provincial food
safety laws, including authorities operating in Punjab, Sindh, Khyber
Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory. These bodies
are responsible for food business licensing, hygiene inspections, sampling
and laboratory testing, enforcement actions, and consumer protection
measures within their jurisdictions.

8

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Industries and Production be pleased to state:

(a) what incentives have been introduced by the Ministry to
encourage domestic and industrial innovation and import
substitution; and

(b) the outcomes of any such schemes launched during Financial
Year 2024-25?
questions.reply:
(a) Government of
Pakistan is providing incentives to the industrial sector through stable and
targeted sectoral policies formulated by Engineering Development Board
(EDB), Ministry of Industries and Production, including the Automotive
Development Policy 2016-2021, Auto Industry Development and Export
Policy 2021-2026, Mobile Device Manufacturing Policy 2020 and the
New Energy Vehicle Policy 2025-2030. These incentives include tariff
rationalization, localization-based concessions, facilitation of new
investment, technology up-gradation, alignment with international
standards, export-oriented capacity enhancement and promotion of
competition to address monopolistic market structures.

The Federal Government, through the Ministry of Industries and
Production (MoI&P) and its executing arm SMEDA, has been running a
Sports Industries Development Centre (SIDC) in Sialkot as a Common
Facility Center to support SMEs with advanced manufacturing facilities,
technical training, laboratory services, and prototype development for
sports goods. The initiative promotes domestic innovation and import
substitution through patented technologies, reverse engineering of
imported machinery, and technology transfer, enabling local enterprises to
produce internationally competitive products and reduce reliance on
foreign equipment.

Pakistan Stone Development Company (PASDEC) has been
established by the Ministry of Industries and Production for the
development of Marble and Granite Sector of Pakistan.

The Company’s core function is to develop the dimensional stone
industry of Pakistan, which is being carried out by introduction of latest
mechanized machinery (Machinery Pools), development of quarries,

9
establishment of state-of-the-art Marble Cities/Industrial Estate and
Common Facility & Training Centers/ Warehouses along with the skill
development to overcome the skilled workforce issues faced by the
industry.

(b) No new incentive schemes were launched during FY 2024-25.
The Ministry focused on implementation and consolidation of existing
policies while formulating new frameworks for strategic sectors, including
automobiles, electronics, solar PV, steel, and battery manufacturing.
Additionally, the Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification Program
(PAVE) Scheme is being operationalized in FY 2025-26 to promote
electric mobility through targeted subsidies and facilitative financing.

Since its inception, SIDC has facilitated to SMEs for
manufacturing of around 11.839 million balls and contributed around USD
68.30 million to the exports from Pakistan & around USD 27 million
import substitution.

 During FY 2024-25, following progress has been made:

 85 SMEs facilitated in Product Development, Technology
Transfer and Trainings.

 2,230,000 number of Bladders, Thermo Football, Basketball,
Rugby Ball and Volleyball were manufactured as per Intl
Market Standards.

 65,000 tennis and squash balls produced.

 Export Development Fund approved Rs. 93.586 Mn funds for
SIDC up-gradation i.e. enhance bladder production, Tennis &
Squash ball unit for enhance of Pakistan export, and Solar
Energy System to reduce the production cost for export
orders. Tendering process for procurement of Machinery &
Equipment and Solar Energy System for upgradation of
Sports Industries Development Centre (SIDC), Sialkot is in
process.

Following initiatives have been undertaken and facilities being
provided to encourage domestic and industrial innovation and import
substitution in the country.

10
1. To attract investor and foster industrializations, dedicated
Marble city has been established at Risalpur with state of art
infrastructure, whereas another Marble City at Loralai is in the planning
phase.

Marble City Risalpur is developed on a total area of 185 acres.
There is total 220 plots of 2, 4 and 8 kanals. Major development works
have been completed. 80 factories have already started their operations.
Moreover, a number of factories (40) are also under construction.

2. PASDEC established Marble City Risalpur (MCR) as the first
purpose-built industrial estate dedicated exclusively to marble and granite
processing and allied industries, wherein, 22 MW dedicated power
infrastructure (including grid connectivity for uninterrupted power supply)
has been provided.

3. PASDEC is actively involved in facilitation in development
of new quarries and the modernization of existing ones through
deployment of mechanized mining machinery on subsidized facilitation
fee basis.

Two machinery Pools have been established in KPK for North
region and in Balochistan for South region to provide latest quarry
machinery on subsidized charge basis to quarry owners. So far more than
135 quarry owners have been facilitated through latest machinery. The
Machinery Pools have played a major role in providing the raw material
for the local processing industry and is a source of production of square
blocks which are exported to different countries.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for Railways be pleased to state:

(a) the total number of marriage grant applications submitted by
widows of Pakistan Railways employees that are currently
pending, including details of long-pending cases;

(b) the steps being taken to expedite the processing of these
pending applications;

(c) the time by which early disbursement of these marriage
grants will be made, particularly employee No.2791290 CC
No.7113 widow’s grant pending case; and

(d) the reason for delay in processing and disbursing the
aforesaid grants?
questions.reply:
(a) At
present, a total of 320 marriage grant applications submitted by widows of
deceased employees of Pakistan Railways are pending. These applications
pertain to the period from 2015 to 2025 and fall under the Prime Minister
Assistance Package for families of deceased Government employees. Each
eligible applicant is entitled to receive a marriage grant of Rs. 0.800
million. Accordingly, the total financial implication involved in respect of
these pending applications amounts to Rs. 255.649 million.

(b) Pakistan Railways has taken all necessary administrative
measures to ensure timely processing of these cases. All applications have
been scrutinized, verified, and duly processed in accordance with the
prescribed rules and policy guidelines. Furthermore, the cases have been
entered into priority lists maintained by the respective Operational
Divisions and Extra Divisional Offices to ensure that payments are
released in an orderly and transparent manner as soon as funds become
available from the Federal Government.

(c) Pakistan Railways remains fully committed to disbursing the
marriage grant to all eligible beneficiaries under the Prime Minister
Assistance Package. It is submitted that, upon release of the required funds
by the Federal Government, the disbursement process will be completed
within a period of 04 to 06 weeks, as all necessary administrative and
procedural formalities have already been finalized. It is further submitted
that an application of Mst. Zareena widow of Muhammad Riaz ex. Skilled
blacksmith (employee No. 2791290) of C&W/Shops Moghalpura
(CC No.7113) who expired on 09-10-2020 is pending in respect of
payment of lump sum grant and cost of plot. The said widow did not apply
for payment of marriage grant as yet. It is clarified that the delay is not due
to procedural or administrative shortcomings, but is solely attributable to
the current financial constraints being faced by Pakistan Railways.

(d) The payment of marriage grant forms an integral component
of the Prime Minister Assistance Package, which also includes lump sum

12
grant, education grant, and provision of residential plots to the families of
deceased employees. Pakistan Railways is currently facing significant
financial constraints due to limited budgetary allocations and competing
liabilities under the said package.

As a result, the overall liability has accumulated to approximately
Rs. 8.190 billion, out of which Rs. 255.649 million pertains specifically to
marriage grant cases. The delay in disbursement is therefore primarily due
to non-availability of funds, and not due to any lapse in processing or
prioritization of cases.

Conclusion / Justification

The Ministry of Railways reiterates that Pakistan Railways
acknowledges its responsibility and is fully committed to making payment
to all eligible applicants under the Prime Minister Assistance Package.
Efforts are being made at the Ministry level to arrange the necessary funds
through budgetary support from the Federal Government and other
financial measures. It is assured that as soon as funds are made available,
all pending payments will be released on priority basis in a transparent and
efficient manner.

questions.question:
Will the Minister for National Food Security and Research be
pleased to state the new policies introduced to increase
agricultural production?
questions.reply:
MNFSR has introduced the Interim National
Wheat Policy (INWP) 2025-26 approved by the Federal Cabinet on
19-11-2025. Due to timely announcement of the INWP wheat sowing area
has been increased by 2.88% in Rabi Season 2025-26 as compared to the
Rabi Season 2024-25. As a result, wheat production is expected to rise by
approximately 1.00 million metric tons compared to last year.

Similarly, the National Agricultural Biotechnology Policy 2025
and the National Seed Policy are under approval process and they will
significantly enhance agricultural productivity in the country through
production of high quality climate resilient seeds of important crops.
